title.zh: 卷三百八十一 列傳第一百四十 范如圭 吳表臣 王居正 晏敦復 黃龜年 程瑀 張闡 洪擬 趙逵
title.en: Volume 381 Biographies 140: Fan Rugui, Wu Biaochen, Wang Juzheng, Yan Dunfu, Huang Guinian, Cheng Yu, Zhang Chan, Hong Ni, Zhao Kui
title.raw: 卷三百八十一 列傳第一百四十 范如圭 吳表臣 王居正 晏敦復 黃龜年 程瑀 張闡 洪擬 趙逵 Volume 381 Biographies 140: Fan Rugui, Wu Biaochen, Wang Juzheng, Yan Dunfu, Huang Guinian, Cheng Yu, Zhang Chan, Hong Ni, Zhao Kui

sentences.zh: 范如圭

translations.literal: Fan Rugui
translations.idiomatic: Fan Rugui

sentences.zh: 范如圭，字伯達，建州建陽人。

translations.literal: Fan Rugui, courtesy name Boda, was a native of Jianyang in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Rugui, styled Boda, came from Jianyang in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從舅氏胡安國受《春秋》。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under his maternal uncle Hu Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 under his maternal uncle Hu Anguo.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，授左從事郎、武安軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Left Attendant Cavalier and military commissioner assessor of the Wu'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he received appointment as Left Attendant Cavalier and assessor to the military commissioner of the Wu'an Army.

sentences.zh: 始至，帥將斬人，如圭白其誤，帥為已署不易也。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, the commander was about to execute someone; Rugui reported that it was a mistake, but the commander, having already signed the order, would not change it.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after his arrival, the commander was about to execute a man. Rugui reported that a mistake had been made, but the commander, having already signed the warrant, refused to reverse it.

sentences.zh: 如圭正色曰：「節下奈何重易一字而輕數人之命？」

translations.literal: Rugui said sternly: "Your Excellency, how can you treat changing one character as weighty yet treat several people's lives as light?"
translations.idiomatic: Rugui replied with stern countenance: "Your Excellency, how can you weigh a single altered character more heavily than several human lives?"

sentences.zh: 帥矍然從之。

translations.literal: The commander, startled, followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Startled awake, the commander accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 自是府中事無大小悉以咨焉。

translations.literal: From then on, matters large and small in the headquarters were all referred to him for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, every matter in the headquarters, great or small, was brought to him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 居數月，以憂去。

translations.literal: After several months, he left office due to mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 辟江東安撫司書寫機宜文字。

translations.literal: He was recruited as secretary for confidential military documents in the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited to draft confidential dispatches for the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 近臣交薦，召試秘書省正字，遷校書郎兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: Close ministers repeatedly recommended him; he was summoned for examination and appointed Corrector in the Secretariat, then promoted to Collator concurrently serving as reviser in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by court intimates, he was summoned for examination and made Corrector in the Secretariat, then promoted to Collator with concurrent duties as reviser in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 秦檜力建和議，金使來，無所於館，將虛秘書省以處之。

translations.literal: Qin Hui forcefully advocated peace talks; when Jin envoys came with nowhere to lodge, they planned to vacate the Secretariat to house them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was pressing hard for a peace settlement. When Jin envoys arrived with no place to stay, the court planned to empty the Secretariat to lodge them there.

sentences.zh: 如圭亟見宰相趙鼎曰：「秘府，謨訓所藏，可使仇敵居之乎？」

translations.literal: Rugui urgently saw Chancellor Zhao Ding and said: "The secret repository holds the counsels and instructions of state — can enemies be allowed to dwell there?"
translations.idiomatic: Rugui sought out Chancellor Zhao Ding at once. "The secret archive holds the counsels and admonitions of the dynasty," he said. "Are we to let our enemies take rooms there?"

sentences.zh: 鼎竦然為改館。

translations.literal: Ding, startled, had the lodging changed.
translations.idiomatic: Startled, Zhao Ding immediately arranged different lodgings.

sentences.zh: 既而金使至悖傲，議多不可從，中外憤鬱。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Jin envoys arrived insolent and arrogant; many of their demands could not be accepted, and anger and resentment filled court and country.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoys arrived, their arrogance made most of their demands unacceptable, and resentment seethed inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 如圭與同省十餘人合議，並疏爭之，既具草，駭遽引卻者眾。

translations.literal: Rugui joined more than ten colleagues of the same office in joint consultation to memorialize in protest together; once the draft was prepared, many, alarmed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui and more than a dozen colleagues in the same office agreed to submit a joint protest. Once the draft was ready, most of them, frightened, fell back.

sentences.zh: 如圭獨以書責檜以曲學倍師、忘讐辱國之罪，且曰：「公不喪心病狂，奈何為此，必遺臭萬世矣！」

translations.literal: Rugui alone wrote a letter rebuking Hui for perverse learning that betrayed the master, forgetting enmity and shaming the state, and said: "Unless you have lost your mind to madness, how can you do this? You will surely leave a stench for ten thousand generations!"
translations.idiomatic: Rugui alone wrote to castigate Hui for warping scholarship to betray his teachers, forgetting old wrongs and shaming the nation. "Unless you have gone mad," he wrote, "how can you do such a thing? Your name will stink for ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 檜怒。

translations.literal: Hui was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Hui flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 草奏與史官六人上之。

translations.literal: The draft memorial, together with six historiographers, was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui and six fellow historiographers submitted the memorial they had drafted.

sentences.zh: 金歸河南地，檜方自以為功。

translations.literal: When the Jin returned the Henan territories, Hui took credit for the achievement himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin restored the Henan territories, Hui congratulated himself on the triumph.

sentences.zh: 如圭輪對，言：「兩京之版圖既入，則九廟、八陵瞻望咫尺，今朝修之使未遣，何以慰神靈、萃民志乎？」

translations.literal: Rugui spoke in rotating audience and said: "Since the maps of the Two Capitals have been recovered, the Nine Temples and Eight Mausoleums are within reach at a glance — yet no envoy has been sent today to restore them; how can the spirits be comforted and the people's will gathered?"
translations.idiomatic: In rotating audience Rugui said: "Now that the Two Capitals are back within our maps, the Nine Temples and Eight Imperial Tombs lie almost within sight — yet we have sent no envoy to restore them. How are we to comfort the ancestral spirits and rally the people's hearts?"

sentences.zh: 帝泫然曰：「非卿不聞此言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with tears: "Were it not for you, I would not have heard these words."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, eyes wet, said: "Had it not been for you, I would never have heard this."

sentences.zh: 即日命宗室士㒟及張燾以行。

translations.literal: That same day he ordered the clansman Shi Yi and Zhang Zhao to proceed on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he ordered the imperial clansman Shi Yi and Zhang Zhao to undertake the mission.

sentences.zh: 檜以不先白己，益怒。

translations.literal: Hui, because he had not been informed beforehand, grew even angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had not been told beforehand, Hui grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 如圭謁告去，奉柩歸葬故鄉，既窆，差主管台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: Rugui requested leave and departed, escorting the coffin home for burial in his native place; after interment, he was assigned to administer the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui took leave, escorted his father's coffin home for burial, and after the interment was appointed administrator of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 杜門十餘歲，起通判邵州，又通判荊南府。

translations.literal: He shut his doors for more than ten years, then was recalled as vice prefect of Shaozhou, and later vice prefect of Jingnan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He kept to his home for more than ten years before being recalled as vice prefect of Shaozhou, then of Jingnan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 荊南舊戶口數十萬，寇亂後無復人跡，時蠲口錢以安集之，百未還一二也。

translations.literal: Jingnan formerly had several hundred thousand registered households; after the bandit turmoil no human traces remained. At the time poll taxes were waived to settle and gather the people, yet not even one or two in a hundred had returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan had once counted several hundred thousand households. After the ravages of war almost no one remained. Poll taxes were waived to coax people back, yet fewer than one or two in a hundred had returned.

sentences.zh: 議者希檜意，遽謂流庸浸復而增之，積逋二十餘萬緡，他負亦數十萬，版曹日下書責償甚急。

translations.literal: Discussants, courting Hui's wish, suddenly claimed that vagrant laborers were gradually returning and increased the levies; accumulated arrears exceeded two hundred thousand strings of cash, and other debts also ran to several hundred thousand; the Revenue Office daily sent documents demanding repayment with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: To curry favor with Hui, officials abruptly declared that displaced laborers were filtering back and raised the levies accordingly. Arrears mounted to more than two hundred thousand strings of cash, with other debts running into hundreds of thousands, and the Revenue Office issued daily demands for payment.

sentences.zh: 如圭白帥，悉奏蠲之。

translations.literal: Rugui reported to the commander and memorialized to remit all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui reported to the military commander and memorialized to have the entire burden remitted.

sentences.zh: 檜死，被旨入對，言：「為治以知人為先，知人以清心寡欲為本。」

translations.literal: After Hui died, he received imperial summons for audience and said: "In governing, knowing men comes first; in knowing men, purity of heart and fewness of desires is fundamental."
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death he was summoned to audience and said: "Good government begins with knowing men, and knowing men begins with a pure heart and restrained desires."

sentences.zh: 語甚切。

translations.literal: His words were very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with great force.

sentences.zh: 又論：「東南不舉子之俗，傷絕人理，請舉漢《胎養令》以全活之，抑亦勾踐生聚報吳之意也。」

translations.literal: He also argued: "The custom in the southeast of not raising children violates human principle; I ask that the Han Fetal-Nurture Edict be invoked to preserve their lives — this also accords with Goujian's idea of multiplying the population to avenge Wu."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "The custom in the southeast of not raising children violates the most basic human bonds; I urge revival of the Han Fetal Nurture Edict to preserve lives—in the spirit of Goujian's policy of replenishing the population to settle accounts with Wu."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised what he said.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「今屯田之法，歲之所獲，官盡征之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Under the present colonization law, the year's harvest is entirely seized by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted: "Under the present garrison-colony system, the state confiscates the entire year's harvest.

sentences.zh: 而田卒賜衣廩食如故，使力穡者絕贏餘之望，惰農者無饑餓之憂，貪小利，失大計，謀近效，妨遠圖，故久無成功。

translations.literal: Yet the colonizing soldiers still received clothing and grain rations as before, so that diligent tillers lost hope of surplus, while lazy farmers had no fear of hunger — grasping small profit, losing the larger plan, scheming for near effect, obstructing distant design; hence long without success.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the colonists still received their usual clothing and grain rations, so hardworking farmers saw no hope of surplus while the idle felt no fear of hunger. Greed for small gains ruined the larger strategy; pursuit of quick results blocked the long view — and that is why the system had never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宜籍荊、淮曠土，畫為丘井，倣古助法，別為科條，令政役法，則農利修而武備飭矣。」

translations.literal: It would be appropriate to register the vacant lands of Jing and Huai, lay them out in well-and-field plots, imitate the ancient aid system, set separate statutes, and harmonize corvée and tax law — then agricultural profit would be restored and military readiness put in order."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed registering the idle lands along the Jing and Huai rivers, dividing them into well-field plots after the ancient aid system, drawing up separate statutes, and aligning corvée and tax levies — so that farming would prosper and defenses would be made sound."

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣提舉江西常平茶監，移利州路提點刑獄，以病請祠。

translations.literal: As Direct Secretarial Aide, he was appointed intendant of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary and Tea Monopoly; transferred to judicial intendant of Lizhou Circuit; he requested temple appointment due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Direct Secretarial Aide, he became intendant of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary and Tea Monopoly, then was transferred to judicial intendant of Lizhou Circuit before requesting a temple appointment on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 時宗藩並建，儲位未定，道路竊有異言。

translations.literal: At the time imperial clansmen were all enfeoffed as princes, the heir was not yet fixed, and whispers of dissent circulated on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the imperial clan had all been enfeoffed, yet the heir remained unsettled, and rumor already murmured in the streets.

sentences.zh: 如圭在遠外，獨深憂之，掇至和、嘉佑間名臣奏章凡三十六篇，合為一書，囊封以獻，請深考群言，仰師成憲，斷以至公勿疑。

translations.literal: Rugui, though far abroad, alone deeply worried; he gathered thirty-six memorials by eminent ministers from the Zhihe and Jiayou periods, combined them into one book, sealed it in a pouch and presented it, asking that the various statements be deeply examined, the established statutes reverently followed, and the decision made with utmost fairness without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Though far from court, Rugui alone brooded over the danger. He collected thirty-six memorials by eminent ministers from the Zhihe and Jiayou reigns, bound them into one volume, sealed it in a pouch, and presented it, urging the throne to weigh every view, follow established precedent, and decide with perfect impartiality and no hesitation.

sentences.zh: 或以越職危之，如圭曰：「以此獲罪，奚憾！」

translations.literal: Some warned him that overstepping his office was dangerous; Rugui said: "If I am punished for this, what regret is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Some warned that he risked punishment for overstepping his office. Rugui replied: "If I suffer for this, what regret would I have?"

sentences.zh: 帝感悟，謂輔臣曰：「如圭可謂忠矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved to understanding and said to his ministers: "Rugui may be called loyal indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the Emperor told his ministers: "Rugui has shown true loyalty."

sentences.zh: 即日下詔以普安郡王為皇子，進封建王。

translations.literal: That same day an edict was issued making the Prince of Pu'an a royal son and advancing him to Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: That very day an edict named the Prince of Pu'an as imperial son and elevated him to Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 復起如圭知泉州。

translations.literal: Rugui was again recalled to serve as prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui was recalled to serve as prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 南外宗官寄治郡中，挾勢為暴，占役禁兵以百數，如圭以法義正之，宗官大沮恨，密為浸潤以去如圭，遂以中旨罷，領祠如故。

translations.literal: Southern Outer Clan officials were administratively attached to the prefecture; relying on power they acted violently, requisitioning several hundred forbidden troops for labor; Rugui corrected them by law and principle; the clan officials greatly resented it and secretly worked influence to remove Rugui, and he was dismissed by confidential edict, retaining his temple appointment as before.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Outer Clan officials lodged in the prefectural seat and abused their power, commandeering scores of palace guards for personal service. Rugui upheld law and justice against them. The clan officials were deeply embittered and quietly worked behind the scenes to remove him; he was dismissed by confidential edict but kept his temple appointment.

sentences.zh: 僦舍邵武以居，士大夫高之，學者多從之質疑。

translations.literal: He rented a dwelling in Shaowu to live in; the scholar-official class held him in esteem, and many students came to him to pose questions.
translations.idiomatic: He rented quarters in Shaowu. Scholar-officials held him in high regard, and many students came to question him on the classics.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十九。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 如圭忠孝誠實，得之於天。

translations.literal: Rugui's loyalty, filial piety, sincerity, and honesty were gifts of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui's loyalty, filial devotion, sincerity, and honesty were innate gifts.

sentences.zh: 其學根於經術，不為無用之文。

translations.literal: His learning was rooted in classical studies; he did not compose useless literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship was grounded in the classics, and he wrote no ornamental fluff.

sentences.zh: 所草具屯田之目數千言，未及上，張浚視師日，奏下其家取之，浚罷，亦不果行。

translations.literal: A draft he composed on colonization totaling several thousand words had not yet been submitted; on the day Zhang Jun inspected the army, an order was sent to his home to retrieve it; when Jun was dismissed, it was still not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He had drafted a colonization proposal of several thousand words but never submitted it. On the day Zhang Jun inspected the armies, an order was sent to his home to retrieve the manuscript. When Jun fell from power, the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，皆書疏議論之語，藏於家。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan, all memorials and policy discussions, kept in the family.
translations.idiomatic: A collection in ten juan — all memorials and policy essays — was kept in the family.

sentences.zh: 子念祖、念德、念茲。

translations.literal: His sons were Nianzu, Niande, and Nianzi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Nianzu, Niande, and Nianzi.

sentences.zh: 吳表臣

translations.literal: Wu Biaochen
translations.idiomatic: Wu Biaochen

sentences.zh: 吳表臣，字正仲，永嘉人。

translations.literal: Wu Biaochen, courtesy name Zhengzhong, was a native of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Biaochen, styled Zhengzhong, came from Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 登大觀三年進士第，擢通州司理。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Daguan and was selected as judicial administrator of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Daguan 3 and was appointed judicial administrator of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘謫居郡中，一見而器之。

translations.literal: Chen Guan was demoted and lived in the prefecture; at one meeting Biaochen recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan, living in the prefecture under demotion, recognized Biaochen's ability at first meeting.

sentences.zh: 盛章者，朱勔黨也，嘗市婢，有武臣強取之，章誣以罪，繫獄。

translations.literal: Sheng Zhang was a member of Zhu Min's faction; he once purchased a maidservant, but a military officer forcibly took her; Zhang falsely charged him with a crime and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Zhang belonged to Zhu Min's faction. He had bought a maidservant when a military officer seized her by force. Zhang framed the officer on a charge and had him jailed.

sentences.zh: 表臣方鞫之，郡將曰：「知有盛待制乎？」

translations.literal: Biaochen was examining the case when the prefectural commander said: "Do you know Assistant Director Sheng?"
translations.idiomatic: While Biaochen was hearing the case, the prefectural commander said: "Do you know Assistant Director Sheng?"

sentences.zh: 表臣佯若不知者，卒直其事。

translations.literal: Biaochen pretended not to know and in the end rendered a just judgment in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Biaochen feigned ignorance and in the end gave a just ruling.

sentences.zh: 累官監察御史，遷右正言。

translations.literal: Through accumulated appointments he became Supervising Censor, then promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Supervising Censor and then Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 高宗詔臺諫條陳大利害，表臣請措置上流以張形勢，安輯淮甸以立藩蔽，擇民兵以守險阻，集海舶以備不虞。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ordered the censorate and remonstrance bureau to set forth major benefits and harms; Biaochen requested arrangements upstream to extend strategic posture, pacification of the Huai region to establish a defensive screen, selection of militia to guard strategic barriers, and gathering of seagoing vessels against unforeseen events.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ordered the censorate and remonstrance offices to lay out the great risks and gains of state. Biaochen urged securing the upper Yangzi to strengthen the strategic posture, stabilizing the Huai region as a defensive buffer, selecting militia to hold the mountain passes, and assembling seagoing vessels against contingencies.

sentences.zh: 其策多見用。

translations.literal: Many of his plans were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 帝方鄉儒術，表臣乞選講官以裨聖德，且於古今成敗、民物情偽，邊防利害，詳熟講究。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then turning toward Confucian learning; Biaochen requested selection of lecture officials to supplement sagely virtue, and thorough investigation of ancient and modern success and failure, the truth and falsity of popular conditions, and the benefits and harms of frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor turned toward Confucian learning, Biaochen asked that lecture officials be chosen to deepen the emperor's virtue, and that the success and failure of past ages, the truth and deception among the people, and the strengths and weaknesses of the frontier be studied thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 由是詔開經筵。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict opened the Classics Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon established the Classics Lectures.

sentences.zh: 邇臣有請用蔡京、王黼之黨者，侍御史沈與求乞明指其人，顯行黜責，執政不悅，奪其言職。

translations.literal: A recent courtier requested employing partisans of Cai Jing and Wang Fu; Remonstrance Officer Shen Yuqiu asked that the persons be explicitly named and openly dismissed and punished; the chief ministers were displeased and stripped him of his remonstrance office.
translations.idiomatic: When a court favorite proposed reemploying men from the factions of Cai Jing and Wang Fu, Supervising Censor Shen Yuqiu demanded that the culprits be named and openly punished. The chief ministers were displeased and stripped him of his remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 表臣爭曰：「臺諫為天子耳目，所以防壅蔽、杜姦邪，若咎其切直而黜之，後誰敢言，非國家福也。

translations.literal: Biaochen protested: "The censorate and remonstrance bureau are the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears, to guard against obstruction and block wickedness; if one is blamed for blunt honesty and dismissed, who afterward will dare speak? This is no blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Biaochen protested: "The censorate and remonstrance offices are the emperor's eyes and ears — they exist to pierce obstruction and cut off corruption. Punish blunt honesty and who will dare speak thereafter? That is no blessing to the realm.

sentences.zh: 請還與求以開言路。」

translations.literal: I ask that Yuqiu be restored to open the path of speech."
translations.idiomatic: Restore Yuqiu and reopen the road of remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 時防秋，議選守邊者，患乏才。

translations.literal: At the time, with autumn defense preparations, when selecting frontier guardians there was worry over lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: With autumn defenses under discussion, the court struggled to find capable men to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 表臣曰：「唐蕭復言于德宗，陳少游任兼將相，首敗臣節，韋皐幕府下僚，獨建忠義，以皐代少遊鎮淮南。

translations.literal: Biaochen said: "In Tang, Xiao Fu spoke to Emperor Dezong: Chen Shaoyou held both ministerial and military posts yet was first to break ministerial integrity; Wei Gao was a low-ranking staff officer yet alone upheld loyalty and righteousness — Gao was made to replace Shaoyou in governing Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Biaochen said: "In Tang, Xiao Fu spoke to Emperor Dezong: Chen Shaoyou held both civil and military rank yet was among the first to betray his oath as a minister, whereas Wei Gao, a junior staff officer, alone upheld loyalty and righteousness—and Gao was appointed to replace Shaoyou in governing Huainan.

sentences.zh: 善惡著明，則天下知逆順之理，初不以皐名賤官卑為疑。

translations.literal: When good and evil are made clear, then all under Heaven knows the principle of obedience and rebellion; at first they did not doubt because Gao's name was obscure and his office low.
translations.idiomatic: When merit and treachery stand plainly revealed, the empire understands which way loyalty runs — and no one hesitated because Gao was obscure and low in rank.

sentences.zh: 今取忠義不屈有已試之驗者，不次而用，豈特可以勸，捍禦方略，亦堪倚仗。」

translations.literal: Now, selecting those of proven loyalty and integrity who have been tested, appointing them out of turn — this not only can encourage others, but their defensive strategies can also be relied upon."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint men of tested loyalty and proven steadfastness regardless of rank, and you do more than encourage others—you gain commanders whose defensive plans can actually be trusted."

sentences.zh: 於是陳敏等十數人浸以錄用。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Min and more than ten others were gradually selected for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min and more than a dozen others were gradually brought into service.

sentences.zh: 久之，以病請補外，以直秘閣知信州。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested outer appointment due to illness; as Direct Secretarial Aide he served as prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing illness, he sought an outside post and was appointed prefect of Xinzhou with the rank of Direct Secretarial Aide.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，召為司勳郎中，遷左司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was summoned as Director of the Bureau of Merits and transferred to the Left Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing he was summoned as Director of the Bureau of Merits and transferred to the Left Section.

sentences.zh: 詔百官陳裕國強兵之策，表臣條十事以獻，曰：蠲稅役以墾閒田，汰懦卒以省兵費，罷添差以澄冗員，停度牒以蕃生齒，拘佃租以防乾沒，委計臣以制邦用，獎有功以厲將帥，招弓手以存舊籍，嚴和買以絕弊幸，簡法令以息瘡痍。

translations.literal: An edict called on all officials to set forth policies to enrich the state and strengthen the army. Biaochen submitted ten items, namely: lighten tax and labor levies to reclaim idle fields; cut weak soldiers to save military expense; abolish supplementary appointments to clarify redundant posts; halt sale of ordination certificates to increase population; bind tenant rents to prevent embezzlement; entrust fiscal commissioners to control state expenditure; reward merit to encourage commanders; recruit archers to preserve old registers; strictly regulate compulsory purchase to end corrupt favor; simplify laws and ordinances to heal society's wounds.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called on all officials to set forth policies to enrich the state and strengthen the army. Biaochen submitted ten items: lighten tax and labor levies to reclaim idle fields; cut weak soldiers to save military expense; abolish supplementary appointments to clarify redundant posts; halt sale of ordination certificates to increase population; bind tenant rents to prevent embezzlement; entrust fiscal commissioners to control state expenditure; reward merit to encourage commanders; recruit archers to preserve old registers; strictly regulate compulsory purchase to end corrupt favor; and simplify laws and ordinances to heal society's wounds.

sentences.zh: 宰相擬表臣為檢正，帝曰：「朕將自用之。」

translations.literal: The chancellor proposed Biaochen as Rectifier; the Emperor said: "I shall employ him myself."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor proposed appointing Biaochen as Rectifier in the Secretariat. The Emperor said: "I mean to use him myself."

sentences.zh: 遂除左司諫。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Left Remonstrator of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made Left Remonstrator in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡安國以論事不合罷，表臣上疏留之。

translations.literal: Drafting Officer Hu Anguo was dismissed because his policy arguments did not accord; Biaochen submitted a memorial asking that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Officer Hu Anguo was dismissed after his policy views fell out of favor; Biaochen memorialized asking that he be kept at court.

sentences.zh: 前宰相朱勝非同都督江淮軍馬，表臣力言都督不可罷。

translations.literal: Former Chancellor Zhu Shengnon disagreed with the overall commander of Jiang-Huai military forces; Biaochen forcefully argued that the overall command should not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Former Chancellor Zhu Shengnon opposed the overall command of Jiang-Huai forces; Biaochen argued forcefully that the post must not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 除侍讀，又累疏爭之，不聽，遂罷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Lecturer-in-Waiting, again repeatedly memorialized in protest, was not heeded, and was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Though appointed Lecturer-in-Waiting, he memorialized repeatedly in protest, was ignored, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 表臣送吏部。

translations.literal: Biaochen was sent to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Biaochen was referred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 授台州黃岩丞，尋除提點浙西刑獄，召為秘書少監，同修《哲宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Huangyan in Taizhou; soon promoted to judicial intendant of Western Zhe; summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat; concurrently compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Assistant Magistrate of Huangyan in Taizhou, then judicial intendant of Western Zhe, summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat, and assigned to compile the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Zhezong》.

sentences.zh: 帝如建康，詔表臣兼留司參議官，除中書舍人、給事中、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went to Jiankang, an edict made Biaochen concurrent Remaining Capital Deliberative Officer; he was appointed Drafting Officer in the Secretariat, Drafting Officer of the Department, and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiankang, Biaochen was named concurrent deliberative officer for the remaining capital and appointed Secretariat Drafting Officer, Drafting Officer of the Department, and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 建、崇二國公就外傅，兼翊善。

translations.literal: The Two Princes of Jian and Chong received outside tutors; he served concurrently as Prince Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes of Jian and Chong received outside tutors, he served concurrently as their tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「二國公誦習甚進，卿力也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Two Princes' recitation and study have progressed greatly — this is your effort."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The two princes have made remarkable progress in their studies — that is your doing."

sentences.zh: 徙禮部侍郎，遷吏部尚書兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, then promoted to Minister of Personnel concurrently Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, then promoted to Minister of Personnel and concurrent Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜欲使使金議地界，指政事堂曰：「歸來可坐此。」

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui wished to send envoys to Jin to negotiate territorial boundaries; pointing to the Hall of Administration he said: "When you return you may sit here."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui wished to send envoys to the Jin to negotiate borders. Pointing to the Hall of Administration he said: "When you return, you may take your seat here."

sentences.zh: 表臣不答。

translations.literal: Biaochen did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Biaochen made no reply.

sentences.zh: 又以議大禮忤意，罷去。

translations.literal: Again, because of disagreement over grand rites he offended the Emperor's wish and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He again fell afoul of the throne over the great rites controversy and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 俄起知婺州。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to serve as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會大水，發常平米振貸之，然後以聞，郡人德之。

translations.literal: When great flood came, he released Ever-Normal Granary rice for relief loans, then reported afterward; the people of the prefecture were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When catastrophic floods struck, he distributed Ever-Normal Granary rice for relief before reporting upward — and the people of the prefecture blessed him for it.

sentences.zh: 課最，除敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: On top evaluation he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Fuwengge Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in performance review, he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Fuwengge Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三歲請祠，進直學士，提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: After three years he requested temple appointment; advanced to Academician Exemplar; appointed administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he requested a temple appointment, was promoted to Academician Exemplar, and made administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 家居數年，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He lived at home several years, then died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement several years and died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 表臣晚號「湛然居士」，自奉無異布衣時，鄉論推其清約。

translations.literal: Biaochen in his later years styled himself "Lay Follower of Stillness"; his personal upkeep was no different from when he was a commoner; local opinion praised his austerity.
translations.idiomatic: In later life Biaochen styled himself "Lay Follower of Stillness." He lived as plainly as he had as a commoner, and local opinion praised his austerity.

sentences.zh: 王居正

translations.literal: Wang Juzheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juzheng

sentences.zh: 王居正，字剛中，揚州人。

translations.literal: Wang Juzheng, courtesy name Gangzhong, was a native of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juzheng, styled Gangzhong, came from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少嗜學，工文辭。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved study and wrote with real skill.

sentences.zh: 入太學，時習《新經》、《字說》者，主司輒置高選，居正語人曰：「窮達自有時，心之是非，可改邪？」

translations.literal: Entering the Imperial Academy, at the time those who studied the New Classics and the Explaining Graphs were always placed in high selection; Juzheng said to others: "Wealth and obscurity have their seasons — can the heart's judgment of right and wrong be altered?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Academy, candidates who mastered the New Classics and Wang Anshi's 《Explaining Graphs》 were always ranked at the top. Juzheng told his companions: "Success and failure come in their season — but can you change what your heart knows to be true?"

sentences.zh: 流落十餘年，司業黃齊得其文，曰：「王佐才也。」

translations.literal: He drifted in obscurity more than ten years; Vice Director Huang Qi obtained his essay and said: "This is the talent of a king's assistant."
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he remained unrecognized. Vice Director Huang Qi read one of his essays and said: "Here is talent fit to assist a king."

sentences.zh: 及同知貢舉，欲擢為首，以風多士，他考官持之，置次選。

translations.literal: When he served as co-examiner for the metropolitan examination, he wished to place him first to set an example for the multitude of scholars; other examiners held back and placed him in the secondary selection.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Qi served as co-examiner for the metropolitan examinations, he wanted to place Juzheng first as an example to scholars everywhere. The other examiners resisted and ranked him in the second tier.

sentences.zh: 調饒州安仁丞、荊州教授，皆不赴。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Assistant Magistrate of Anren in Raozhou and Professor in Jingzhou — he went to neither.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments as Assistant Magistrate of Anren in Raozhou and as Professor in Jingzhou both came — and he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 大名、鎮江兩帥交辟教授府學，亦不就。

translations.literal: The two commanders of Daming and Zhenjiang repeatedly recruited him as academy professor — he also did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders of Daming and Zhenjiang both repeatedly invited him to serve as academy professor — and he declined those as well.

sentences.zh: 范宗尹薦於朝，召至，謂宗尹曰：「時危如此，公不極所學，拔元元塗炭中，尚誰待？

translations.literal: Fan Zongyin recommended him to the court. When summoned, [the emperor] said to Fan: "Times are as perilous as this—will you not bring all your learning to bear and lift the common people from fire and water? Who else are we waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin recommended Wang Juzheng to the court. When Juzheng was summoned, the emperor said to Fan, "Times are this perilous—will you not bring all your learning to bear and lift the people from misery? Who else are we waiting for?

sentences.zh: 居正避寇陽羨山間，勉出見公，一道此意爾。」

translations.literal: Juzheng had been avoiding bandits in the Yangxian hills. Reluctantly he came out to see Fan and expressed this sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had been hiding from the invaders in the hills of Yangxian. Reluctantly he came out to see Fan and spoke to this effect."

sentences.zh: 宗尹愧謝。

translations.literal: Fan apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Fan apologized, abashed.

sentences.zh: 入對，奏：「昔人有云：『君以為難，易將至矣。』

translations.literal: At audience he memorialized: "A man of old said: 'When the ruler considers something difficult, ease is about to arrive.'
translations.idiomatic: At audience he memorialized, "A man of old said, 'When the ruler treats something as difficult, ease is about to arrive.'

sentences.zh: 今日之事，朝廷皆曰難，則當有易為之理。

translations.literal: In today's affairs, when the court says everything is difficult, there ought to be a principle by which difficulty becomes ease.
translations.idiomatic: In today's affairs, when the whole court calls everything difficult, there ought to be some way to make the difficult easy.

sentences.zh: 然國勢日弱，敵氣日驕，何邪？

translations.literal: Yet the national strength weakens day by day and the enemy grows prouder day by day—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the state grows weaker by the day and the enemy grows prouder by the day—why?

sentences.zh: 蓋昔人於難者勉強為之，今以為難，不復有所為，以俟天意自回，強敵自斃也。

translations.literal: Former men, faced with difficulty, exerted themselves to act. Today, calling things difficult, they no longer act at all, waiting for Heaven's will to turn of itself and the strong foe to perish of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old, when things were hard, still forced themselves to act. Today people call things hard and then do nothing, waiting for Heaven to turn of its own accord and the strong enemy to die on his own.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，以為難者十五六，至靖康與宣和孰難？

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, fifteen or sixteen out of twenty considered things difficult. Between Jingkang and Xuanhe, which was harder?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, fifteen or sixteen out of every twenty men treated affairs as hopeless. Between Jingkang and Xuanhe, which was harder?

sentences.zh: 靖康末，以為難者十八九，至建炎與靖康孰難？

translations.literal: At the end of Jingkang, eighteen or nineteen out of twenty considered things difficult. Between Jianyan and Jingkang, which was harder?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jingkang, eighteen or nineteen out of every twenty did the same. Between Jianyan and Jingkang, which was harder?

sentences.zh: 由此而言，今日雖難於前日，安知他日不難於今日？

translations.literal: From this perspective, though today is harder than yesterday, who knows that tomorrow may not be harder than today?
translations.idiomatic: By this reckoning, though today is harder than yesterday, who can say tomorrow will not be harder still?

sentences.zh: 蓋宣和以為難，故有靖康之禍；

translations.literal: Because Xuanhe treated things as difficult, there came the Jingkang calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Because Xuanhe treated things as difficult, the Jingkang disaster followed;

sentences.zh: 靖康以為難，故有今日之憂。

translations.literal: because Jingkang treated things as difficult, there is today's distress.
translations.idiomatic: because Jingkang treated things as difficult, we have today's distress.

sentences.zh: 今而亦云，臣有所不忍聞。」

translations.literal: To say the same now—I cannot bear to hear it."
translations.idiomatic: To hear the same said now—I cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉之，諭宗尹曰：「如王居正人才，歲月間得一人亦幸矣。」

translations.literal: Gaozong praised this and told Fan Zongyin: "Talent like Wang Juzheng's—if we gain one such man in the space of months, that is already fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong praised the memorial and told Fan Zongyin, "For talent like Wang Juzheng's, to gain one man in the space of months is already good fortune."

sentences.zh: 除太常博士，遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Doctor of the Grand Imperial Sacrificial Office and promoted to Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Doctor of the Grand Imperial Sacrificial Office and promoted to Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建議合祭天地於明堂，請奉太祖、太宗配，宗尹是之，議遂定，天地復合祭。

translations.literal: He proposed combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Bright Hall, requesting that Taizu and Taizong be enshrined as associates. Fan Zongyin agreed, the proposal was settled, and Heaven and Earth were again worshipped together.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that Heaven and Earth be worshipped together in the Bright Hall, with Taizu and Taizong enshrined as associates. Fan Zongyin agreed, the measure was adopted, and the joint rite was restored.

sentences.zh: 侍御史沈與求劾宗尹，因及居正，宗尹去，居正乞補外，不許。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Censor Shen Yuqiu impeached Fan Zongyin and implicated Juzheng. Fan departed; Juzheng requested an outside appointment but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Censor Shen Yuqiu impeached Fan Zongyin and implicated Juzheng. Fan left office; Juzheng asked to serve outside the capital but was refused.

sentences.zh: 撫州守高衛言甘露降於州之祥符觀，為圖以獻。

translations.literal: Gao Wei, prefect of Fuzhou, reported that sweet dew had fallen at the Xiangfu Temple in the prefecture and presented a diagram of it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei, prefect of Fuzhou, reported that sweet dew had fallen at the prefecture's Xiangfu Temple and presented a diagram of the event.

sentences.zh: 居正論今日恐非天降祥瑞之時，卻其圖。

translations.literal: Juzheng argued that the present was hardly a time for heavenly auspices and rejected the diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng argued that the present was hardly a time for heavenly omens of good fortune and rejected the diagram.

sentences.zh: 試太常少卿兼修政局參議，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He was tried as Vice-Director of the Grand Imperial Sacrificial Office with concurrent duty as deliberator of the Bureau for Revision of Administrative Regulations, then promoted to Gentleman-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was tried as Vice-Director of the Grand Imperial Sacrificial Office with concurrent duty as deliberator in the Bureau for Revision of Administrative Regulations, then promoted to Gentleman-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝方鄉規諫，居正次前世聽納事為《集諫》十五卷，以廣帝意。

translations.literal: The emperor was then inclined toward admonition. Juzheng compiled previous instances of rulers heeding remonstrance into fifteen scrolls entitled Collected Remonstrances to broaden the emperor's understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then inclined to accept remonstrance. Juzheng compiled earlier instances of rulers heeding advice into fifteen scrolls entitled Collected Remonstrances, to broaden the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 詔以時務訪群臣，居正獻疏數千言，論省費尤切，曰：「宋興百七十三年矣，所行多彌文之事。

translations.literal: An edict solicited the ministers' views on current affairs. Juzheng submitted a memorial of several thousand characters, speaking most urgently on economy of expenditure, saying: "The Song has risen one hundred seventy-three years, and what is practiced is mostly elaborate formality.
translations.idiomatic: An edict solicited the ministers' views on current affairs. Juzheng submitted a memorial several thousand characters long, speaking most urgently on cutting expenses. He said, "The Song has stood one hundred seventy-three years, yet what is practiced is mostly ornamental ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今陛下所至曰行在，於一日二日少駐蹕之頃，欲盡為向者百七十三年之事，非所謂知變也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's present seat is called the Mobile Court. In the brief halt of a day or two, to wish to do everything that belonged to those one hundred seventy-three years is not what is meant by knowing how to adapt.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's present seat is called the Mobile Court. In the brief pause of a day or two, to try to do everything that belonged to those one hundred seventy-three years is not what is meant by knowing how to adapt.

sentences.zh: 夫不知隨時以省事，而乃隨事以省費，故今日例有減半之說，究其實未始不重費。

translations.literal: Not knowing how to economize affairs according to the times, but instead economizing expenses item by item—hence today's talk of cutting everything in half; examined in fact, it has never truly reduced expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing how to cut work according to the times, but instead cutting costs item by item—hence today's talk of halving every expense; in fact it has never truly made things cheaper.

sentences.zh: 願詔大臣計百事之實而論定之，苟非禦寇備敵，任賢使能，振恤百姓，一切姑置，則費省而國裕。」

translations.literal: I ask that Your Majesty charge the great ministers to calculate the reality of every affair and settle it. If it is not repelling invaders, preparing against the enemy, appointing the worthy and employing the capable, or reviving and relieving the people—let all such matters be set aside for now—then expenses will be saved and the state will be ample."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty charge the great ministers to reckon the real cost of every affair and settle it. Whatever is not repelling invaders, preparing against the enemy, appointing the worthy, employing the capable, or reviving and relieving the people should be set aside for now. Then expenses will fall and the state will be secure."

sentences.zh: 居正素與秦檜善，檜為執政，與居正論天下事甚銳，既相，所言皆不酬。

translations.literal: Juzheng had long been on good terms with Qin Hui. When Qin held power, he and Juzheng debated state affairs keenly. Once he became chief councillor, none of Juzheng's proposals was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had long been friendly with Qin Hui. While Qin held power, he and Juzheng debated state affairs sharply. Once Qin became chief councillor, none of Juzheng's proposals was heeded.

sentences.zh: 居正疾其詭，見帝言曰：「秦檜嘗語臣：『中國人惟當著衣啖飯，共圖中興。』

translations.literal: Juzheng resented his duplicity. Seeing the emperor he said: "Qin Hui once told me: 'Chinese people need only dress and eat and together strive for restoration.'
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng resented his duplicity. Seeing the emperor he said, "Qin Hui once told me, 'We Chinese need only dress and eat and together strive for restoration.'

sentences.zh: 臣心服其言。

translations.literal: I was convinced by his words.
translations.idiomatic: I was convinced by what he said.

sentences.zh: 又自謂：『使檜為相數月，必聳動天下。』

translations.literal: He also said of himself: 'If I were chief councillor for a few months, I would surely stir the whole empire.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said of himself, 'If I were chief councillor for a few months, I would surely stir the whole empire.'

sentences.zh: 今為相施設止是，願陛下以臣所聞問檜。」

translations.literal: Now that he is chief councillor, his measures go no further than this. I ask Your Majesty to put what I have heard to Qin Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is chief councillor, his measures go no further than this. I ask Your Majesty to put what I have heard to Qin Hui directly."

sentences.zh: 檜銜之，出居正知婺州。

translations.literal: Qin bore a grudge and had Juzheng sent out as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin bore a grudge and had Juzheng sent out as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 州貢羅，舊制歲萬匹，崇寧後增五倍，建炎中減為二萬。

translations.literal: The prefecture's tribute of gauze silk had formerly been ten thousand bolts yearly. After Chongning it was increased fivefold; in the Jianyan period it was reduced to twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's tribute of gauze silk had formerly been ten thousand bolts a year. After Chongning it was increased fivefold; during Jianyan it was reduced to twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 至是，主計者請復崇寧之數，居正力言於朝，戶部督趣愈峻，居正置檄不行，語其屬曰：「吾願身坐，不以累諸君。」

translations.literal: At this time those in charge of accounts asked to restore the Chongning figure. Juzheng forcefully stated his case at court. The Ministry of Revenue pressed ever more urgently; Juzheng set the dispatch aside and did not act, telling his staff: "I am willing to bear punishment myself and not involve you all."
translations.idiomatic: At this time those in charge of accounts asked to restore the Chongning quota. Juzheng forcefully argued against it at court. The Ministry of Revenue pressed ever harder; Juzheng set the order aside and did not carry it out, telling his staff, "I am willing to bear punishment myself and not involve any of you."

sentences.zh: 呼吏為文書付之曰：「即有譴，以此自解。」

translations.literal: He called a clerk to draft a document and gave it to them, saying: "If there is blame, use this to exonerate yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: He had a clerk draft a written statement and gave it to them, saying, "If blame falls, use this to clear yourselves."

sentences.zh: 復手疏「五不可」以聞。

translations.literal: He also submitted in his own hand a memorial on "Five Reasons Why Not" to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted in his own hand a memorial titled "Five Reasons Why Not" to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔如建炎中數。

translations.literal: An edict followed the Jianyan figure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed the quota at the Jianyan figure.

sentences.zh: 漕司市御炭，須胡桃文、鵓鴿色者，居正曰：「民以炭自業者，率居山谷，安知所謂胡桃文、鵓鴿色耶？」

translations.literal: The transport commissioner was purchasing imperial charcoal and required grain-patterns like walnut and the hue of the spotted dove. Juzheng said: "People who live by charcoal mostly dwell in mountain valleys—how would they know what is meant by walnut grain or spotted-dove color?"
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner was purchasing imperial charcoal and required patterns like walnut grain and the color of the spotted dove. Juzheng said, "People who live by making charcoal mostly dwell in mountain valleys—how would they know what walnut grain or spotted-dove color means?"

sentences.zh: 入朝以聞，詔止之。

translations.literal: On entering court he reported this; an edict halted the practice.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered court and reported this, an edict halted the practice.

sentences.zh: 召為太常少卿，遷起居舍人兼權中書舍人、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Vice-Director of the Grand Imperial Sacrificial Office and promoted to Gentleman of Diary-writing with concurrent acting duty as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and compiler of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice-Director of the Grand Imperial Sacrificial Office and promoted to Gentleman of Diary-writing with concurrent acting duty as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and compiler of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 帝欲遷趙令峸大中大夫，居正奏：「官非侍從不可轉，此祖宗法，若令峸以庶官得遷，則宗室為承宣者，不旋踵求為節度，何以卻之？」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to promote Zhao Lingqi to Grandee of Palace Attendance. Juzheng memorialized: "One who is not among the personal attendants may not be transferred to such a post—this is ancestral law. If Lingqi may be promoted from a common office, then every prince who is commissioner of appearance will before long seek to be military commissioner—how can we refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to promote Zhao Lingqi to Grandee of Palace Attendance. Juzheng memorialized, "One who is not among the personal attendants may not be transferred to such a post—this is ancestral law. If Lingqi may be promoted from an ordinary office, then every imperial clansman who is commissioner of appearance will soon seek to become military commissioner—how can we refuse them?"

sentences.zh: 遂寢其命。

translations.literal: The appointment was therefore shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was therefore shelved.

sentences.zh: 上書人陳東、歐陽澈已贈官，居正乞重貶黃潛善、汪伯彥，以彰二子殺身成仁之美。

translations.literal: The petitioners Chen Dong and Ouyang Che had already been granted posthumous honors. Juzheng asked that Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan be heavily demoted, to highlight the two men's beauty of dying for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The petitioners Chen Dong and Ouyang Che had already been granted posthumous honors. Juzheng asked that Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan be heavily demoted, to set off the two men's sacrifice for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 大將張俊遣卒至彭澤，卒故縣吏，怙俊勢侵辱令，令郭彥恭械之，俊訴於朝，帝為罷彥恭。

translations.literal: The great general Zhang Jun sent a soldier to Pengze. The soldier had formerly been a county clerk and, relying on Jun's power, insulted the magistrate. Magistrate Guo Yangong had him shackled. Jun complained at court and the emperor dismissed Yangong.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Zhang Jun sent a soldier to Pengze. The soldier had formerly been a county clerk and, relying on Jun's power, insulted the magistrate. Magistrate Guo Yangong had him put in fetters. Jun complained at court and the emperor dismissed Yangong.

sentences.zh: 居正言：「彥恭不畏強禦，無可罪。」

translations.literal: Juzheng said: "Yangong did not fear the strong—there is no offense."
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng said, "Yangong did not fear the powerful—he committed no offense."

sentences.zh: 俊又乞免徭役，居正言：「兵興以來，士大夫及勳戚家賦役與編戶均，蓋欲貴賤上下，共濟國事，以寬民力，俊反不能體此乎？」

translations.literal: Jun also asked exemption from corvée and tax service. Juzheng said: "Since the war began, gentry and merit households have shared tax and corvée with registered households equally—the aim was that high and low together should sustain the state's affairs and ease the people's burden. Can Jun not grasp even this?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun also asked to be exempted from corvée and tax service. Juzheng said, "Since the war began, gentry and merit households have shared tax and corvée with ordinary households—the aim was that high and low together should sustain the state and ease the people's burden. Can Jun not grasp even this?"

sentences.zh: 和州請蠲進奉大禮絹，居正言：「大禮進奉，乃臣子享上之誠，初非朝廷取于百姓之物，若察民力無所從出，不能預降旨蠲之，至使州縣自陳，已為非是，乞速如所請。」

translations.literal: Hezhou requested remission of the silk tribute for the grand rites. Juzheng said: "The grand-rites tribute is the sincerity of subjects toward their ruler; it is not in the first place something the court takes from the people. If one sees that the people's strength has no source from which to meet it, one ought beforehand to issue an edict remitting it. To wait until counties and prefectures petition on their own is already wrong; I ask that the request be granted at once."
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou requested remission of the silk tribute for the grand rites. Juzheng said, "The grand-rites tribute is the sincerity of subjects toward their ruler; it is not in the first place something the court takes from the people. If one sees that the people have no means to meet it, one ought to issue an edict remitting it beforehand. To wait until counties and prefectures petition on their own is already wrong; I ask that the request be granted at once."

sentences.zh: 除目有自中出者，居正奏：「近習請託，進擬不自朝廷，所繫非輕。」

translations.literal: Appointments issued from within [the palace]: Juzheng memorialized: "Favorites petition and nominations do not come from the court—the matter is no light one."
translations.idiomatic: When appointments issued from within the palace, Juzheng memorialized, "Favorites petition for posts and nominations do not come from the court—the matter is no light one."

sentences.zh: 因錄皇佑詔書以進。

translations.literal: He therefore copied in and submitted the edict of the Huangyou era.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore copied out and submitted the edict of the Huangyou era.

sentences.zh: 帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 兼權直學士院，又除兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He held concurrent acting duty in the Hanlin Academy and was further appointed Vice-Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He held concurrent acting duty in the Hanlin Academy and was further appointed Vice-Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 入對，以所論王安石父子之言不合於道者，裒得四十二篇，名曰《辨學》，上之。

translations.literal: At audience he collected forty-two passages in which Wang Anshi and his son had spoken contrary to the Way, entitled Discerning Learning, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he collected forty-two passages in which Wang Anshi and his son had spoken contrary to the Way, entitled the work Discerning Learning, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下惡安石之學，嘗於聖心灼見，其弊安在？」

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty detests the learning of Anshi. You have plainly seen in your sacred mind where its harm lies?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Your Majesty detests the learning of Anshi. You have plainly seen in your own mind where its harm lies?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「安石之學，雜以伯道，欲效商鞅富國強兵，今日之禍，人徒知蔡京、王黼之罪，而不知生於安石。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Anshi's learning, mixed with Legalist doctrine, sought to emulate Shang Yang in enriching the state and strengthening the army. Today's disaster—people know only the guilt of Cai Jing and Wang Fu, and do not know that it arose from Anshi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Anshi's learning, mixed with Legalist doctrine, sought to emulate Shang Yang in enriching the state and strengthening the army. Today's disaster—people know only the guilt of Cai Jing and Wang Fu, and do not see that it arose from Anshi."

sentences.zh: 居正曰：「安石得罪萬世者不止此。」

translations.literal: Juzheng said: "What makes Anshi guilty before ten thousand generations is not limited to this."
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng said, "What makes Anshi guilty before ten thousand generations is not limited to this."

sentences.zh: 因陳安石釋經無父無君者。

translations.literal: He then set forth how Anshi, in interpreting the classics, had been without father and without lord.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth how Anshi, in interpreting the classics, had been without father and without lord.

sentences.zh: 帝作色曰：「是豈不害名教邪？

translations.literal: The emperor's color changed: "Does this not harm the teaching of names and relationships?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed. "Does this not harm the teaching of names and relationships?

sentences.zh: 孟子所謂邪說，正謂是矣。」

translations.literal: What Mencius called heterodox doctrine—this is exactly it."
translations.idiomatic: What Mencius called heterodox doctrine—this is exactly it."

sentences.zh: 居正退，序帝語繫於《辨學》首。

translations.literal: Juzheng withdrew and placed the emperor's words at the head of Discerning Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng withdrew and placed the emperor's words at the head of Discerning Learning.

sentences.zh: 出知饒州，尋改吉州。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Raozhou, then transferred to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Raozhou, then transferred to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 侍御史謝祖信劾居正兇暴詭詐，傾陷大臣，罷官，屏居括蒼三載。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Censor Xie Zuxin impeached Juzheng for violence, deceit, and ruining great ministers. He was dismissed and lived in seclusion at Kuocang for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Censor Xie Zuxin impeached Juzheng for violence, deceit, and ruining great ministers. He was dismissed and lived in seclusion at Kuocang for three years.

sentences.zh: 其弟駕部郎居修入對，帝曰：「卿兄今安在？

translations.literal: His younger brother Juxiu, Gentleman of the Transport Ministry, attended audience. The emperor said: "Where is your elder brother now?
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Juxiu, Gentleman of the Transport Ministry, attended audience. The emperor said, "Where is your elder brother now?

sentences.zh: 行大用矣。」

translations.literal: He will soon be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: He will soon be greatly employed."

sentences.zh: 中書舍人劉大中侍帝，論制誥，帝曰：「王居正極得詞臣體。」

translations.literal: Drafting Secretary Liu Dazhong attended the emperor and discussed edict composition. The emperor said: "Wang Juzheng fully possesses the style of a drafting minister."
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Secretary Liu Dazhong attended the emperor and discussed edict composition. The emperor said, "Wang Juzheng fully possesses the style of a drafting minister."

sentences.zh: 侍御史蕭振論守令賢否，帝舉居正守婺免貢羅、御炭事，曰：「守臣愛百姓皆如此，朕復何憂。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance Censor Xiao Zhen discussed whether prefects and magistrates were worthy. The emperor cited Juzheng's governing of Wu and exemption from silk tribute and imperial charcoal, saying: "If every prefect loved the people as he did, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Censor Xiao Zhen discussed whether prefects and magistrates were worthy. The emperor cited Juzheng's governing of Wu and his refusal of silk tribute and imperial charcoal, saying, "If every prefect loved the people as he did, what would I have to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 起知溫州。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時檜專國，居正自知不為所容，以目疾請祠，杜門，言不及時事，客至談論經、史而已。

translations.literal: At that time Qin monopolized the state. Juzheng knew he would not be tolerated. Citing eye disease he requested a sinecure, shut his doors, and spoke of current affairs no more; when guests came he discussed only the classics and history.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin monopolized the state. Juzheng knew he would not be tolerated. Citing eye disease he requested a sinecure, shut his doors, and spoke of current affairs no more; when guests came he discussed only the classics and history.

sentences.zh: 檜終忌之，風中丞何鑄劾居正為趙鼎汲引，欺世盜名，奪職奉祠，凡十年。

translations.literal: Qin still hated him and prompted Censor-in-Chief He Zhu to impeach Juzheng as promoted by Zhao Ding—deceiving the age and stealing a name. His office was stripped and he held a sinecure for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Qin still hated him and prompted Censor-in-Chief He Zhu to impeach Juzheng as promoted by Zhao Ding—deceiving the age and stealing a name. His office was stripped and he held a sinecure for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 檜死，復故職。

translations.literal: When Qin died, his former post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin died, his former post was restored.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十一年卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 居正儀觀豐偉，聲音洪暢。

translations.literal: Juzheng's bearing was tall and imposing and his voice resounding.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was tall and imposing in appearance and resounding in voice.

sentences.zh: 奉祿班兄弟宗族，無留者。

translations.literal: He distributed his salary to brothers and clansmen—none was left behind.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed his salary among brothers and clansmen—none was left out.

sentences.zh: 郊祀恩以任其弟居厚，及卒，季子猶布衣。

translations.literal: At the suburban-sacrifice grace he used his privilege for his brother Juhou. When he died, his youngest son was still in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: At the grace granted after the suburban sacrifice he used his privilege for his brother Juhou. When he died, his youngest son was still in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 其學根據《六經》，楊時器之，出所著《三經義辨》示居正曰：「吾舉其端，子成吾志。」

translations.literal: His learning was rooted in the Six Classics. Yang Shi valued him and showed him his Three Classics Discerning Meaning, saying: "I begin the thread—you finish my intent."
translations.idiomatic: His learning was rooted in the Six Classics. Yang Shi valued him and showed him his Three Classics Discerning Meaning, saying, "I begin the thread—you finish my intent."

sentences.zh: 居正感厲，首尾十載為《書辨學》十三卷，《詩辨學》二十卷，《周禮辨學》五卷，《辨學外集》一卷。

translations.literal: Juzheng was stirred and worked for ten years at the beginning and end, producing Discerning Learning of the Documents in thirteen scrolls, Discerning Learning of the Odes in twenty scrolls, Discerning Learning of the Rites of Zhou in five scrolls, and Outer Collected Discerning Learning in one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was stirred and worked for ten years from beginning to end, producing Discerning Learning of the Documents in thirteen scrolls, Discerning Learning of the Odes in twenty scrolls, Discerning Learning of the Rites of Zhou in five scrolls, and Outer Collected Discerning Learning in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 居正既進其書七卷，而楊時《三經義辨》亦列秘府，二書既行，天下遂不復言王氏學。

translations.literal: After Juzheng had submitted seven scrolls of his book and Yang Shi's Three Classics Discerning Meaning was also placed in the secret repository, once the two books circulated the empire no longer spoke of the Wang family learning.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng had submitted seven scrolls of his book and Yang Shi's Three Classics Discerning Meaning was also placed in the imperial library, once the two works circulated the empire no longer spoke of the Wang family learning.

sentences.zh: 晏敦復

translations.literal: Yan Dunfu
translations.idiomatic: Yan Dunfu

sentences.zh: 晏敦復，字景初，丞相殊之曾孫。

translations.literal: Yan Dunfu, styled Jingchu, was a great-grandson of Chief Councillor Yan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Dunfu, styled Jingchu, was a great-grandson of Chief Councillor Yan Shu.

sentences.zh: 少學于程頤，頤奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Cheng Yi, who considered him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Cheng Yi, who considered him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為御史臺檢法官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became investigating legal officer of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and became investigating legal officer of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，大臣薦，召試館職，不就。

translations.literal: In the early Shaoxing period, great ministers recommended him. He was summoned to trial for an academy post but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shaoxing period, great ministers recommended him. He was summoned to trial for an academy post but declined.

sentences.zh: 特命祠部郎官，遷吏部，以守法忤呂頤浩，出知貴溪縣。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel. For upholding the law he offended Lü Yihao and was sent out as magistrate of Guixi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel. For upholding the law he offended Lü Yihao and was sent out as magistrate of Guixi County.

sentences.zh: 會有為敦復直其事者，改通判臨江軍，召為吏部郎官、左司諫、權給事中，為中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: When someone vindicated Dunfu's case, he was changed to administrative vice-commissioner of Linjiang Army, recalled as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Left Remonstrator, and acting Supervising Censor, and served as rectifier of the general affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery offices.
translations.idiomatic: When someone vindicated Dunfu's case, he was changed to administrative vice-commissioner of Linjiang Army, recalled as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Left Remonstrator, and acting Supervising Censor, and served as rectifier of the general affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery offices.

sentences.zh: 淮西宣撫使劉光世請以淮東私田易淮西田，帝許之。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Liu Guangshi of Huai West requested to exchange his private fields in Huai East for fields in Huai West. The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Liu Guangshi of Huai West requested to exchange his private fields in Huai East for fields in Huai West. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 敦復言：「光世帥一道，未聞為朝廷措置毫髮，乃先易私畝。

translations.literal: Dunfu said: "Guangshi commands a whole circuit and has not been heard to arrange a hair's breadth for the court—yet he first exchanges private acres.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu said, "Guangshi commands a whole circuit and has not been heard to arrange a hair's breadth for the court—yet he first exchanges private acres.

sentences.zh: 比者岳飛屬官以私事干朝廷，飛請加罪，中外稱美，謂有古賢將風。

translations.literal: Recently an officer under Yue Fei improperly petitioned the court on a private matter; Yue asked that he be punished, and within and without the court praised this, saying he had the wind of the ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Recently an officer under Yue Fei improperly petitioned the court on a private matter; Yue asked that he be punished, and within and without the court praised this, saying he had the bearing of the worthy generals of old.

sentences.zh: 光世自處必不在飛下，乞以臣言示光世，且令經理淮南，收撫百姓，以為定都建康計，中興有期，何患私計之未便。」

translations.literal: Guangshi surely does not place himself below Yue. I ask that my words be shown to Guangshi and that he be ordered to manage Huainan, gather and comfort the people, as part of the plan to fix the capital at Jiankang—then restoration will have its term; why worry that private schemes are not yet convenient?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi surely does not place himself below Yue. I ask that my words be shown to Guangshi and that he be ordered to manage Huainan, gather and comfort the people, as part of the plan to fix the capital at Jiankang—then restoration will have its term; why worry that private schemes are not yet convenient?"

sentences.zh: 權吏部侍郎兼詳定一司敕令。

translations.literal: Acting Vice-Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty revising the statutes of the One Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was acting Vice-Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty revising the statutes of the One Bureau.

sentences.zh: 渡江後，庶事草創，凡四選格法多所裁定。

translations.literal: After crossing the river, in the midst of founding everything anew, he adjudicated many matters of the four-selection regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river, in the midst of founding everything anew, he adjudicated many matters of the four-selection regulations.

sentences.zh: 敦復素剛嚴，居吏部，請謁不行，銓綜平允，除給事中。

translations.literal: Dunfu was by nature stern and severe. In the Ministry of Personnel he would not accept petitions; his evaluations were even-handed, and he was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu was by nature stern and severe. In the Ministry of Personnel he would not accept petitions; his evaluations were even-handed, and he was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 冬至節，旨下禮部，取度牒四百充賜予。

translations.literal: At the Winter Solstice an instruction went to the Ministry of Rites to take four hundred ordination certificates for bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: At the Winter Solstice an instruction went to the Ministry of Rites to take four hundred ordination certificates for bestowal.

sentences.zh: 敦復奏：「兵興費廣，凡可助用度者尤當惜，矧兩宮在遠，陛下當此令節，欲奉一觴為萬歲壽不可得，有司乃欲舉平時例行慶賜乎？」

translations.literal: Dunfu memorialized: "With war, expense is vast—anything that can assist the budget should especially be spared. Moreover the Two Palaces are far away; on this festive day Your Majesty cannot offer a cup for ten thousand years of life—are the officials yet intending to carry out the routine celebratory grants of ordinary times?"
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu memorialized, "With war, expense is vast—anything that can assist the budget should especially be spared. Moreover the Two Palaces are far away; on this festive day Your Majesty cannot offer a cup for ten thousand years of life—are the officials yet intending to carry out the routine celebratory grants of ordinary times?"

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 有卒失宣帖，得中旨給據，太醫吳球得旨免試，敦復奏：「一卒之微，乃至上瀆聖聰，醫官免試，皆壞成法。

translations.literal: A soldier lost his dispatch slip yet received an inner instruction granting credentials; the court physician Wu Qiu received an instruction exempting him from examination. Dunfu memorialized: "For one soldier so slight to reach the point of sullying the imperial ear, and for a medical officer to be exempted from examination—both destroy established law.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier lost his dispatch slip yet received an inner instruction granting credentials; the court physician Wu Qiu received an instruction exempting him from examination. Dunfu memorialized, "For one soldier so slight to reach the point of sullying the imperial ear, and for a medical officer to be exempted from examination—both destroy established law.

sentences.zh: 自崇寧、大觀以來，姦人欺罔，臨事取旨，謂之『暗嬴指揮』，紀綱敗壞，馴致危亂，正蹈前弊，不可長也。」

translations.literal: Since Chongning and Daguan, wicked men deceived and, on each affair, took instructions—calling them 'covert peremptory directives'—until discipline collapsed and disorder followed step by step. To tread the former evil again must not be allowed to grow."
translations.idiomatic: Since Chongning and Daguan, wicked men deceived the throne and, on each affair, took private instructions—calling them 'covert peremptory directives'—until discipline collapsed and disorder followed step by step. To tread that evil again must not be allowed."

sentences.zh: 汪伯彥子召嗣除江西監司，敦復論：「伯彥姦庸誤國，其子素無才望，難任澄清。」

translations.literal: Wang Boyan's son Zhaosi was appointed surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi. Dunfu argued: "Boyan was treacherous and mediocre and ruined the state; his son has never had talent or repute and cannot bear the task of purification."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boyan's son Zhaosi was appointed surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi. Dunfu argued, "Boyan was treacherous and mediocre and ruined the state; his son has never had talent or repute and cannot bear the task of purification."

sentences.zh: 改知袁州。

translations.literal: [Zhaosi] was changed to prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosi was changed to prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「召嗣既不可為監司，亦不可為守臣。」

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Zhaosi can be neither surveillance commissioner nor prefect."
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized, "Zhaosi can be neither surveillance commissioner nor prefect."

sentences.zh: 居右省兩月，論駁凡二十四事，議者憚之。

translations.literal: In the Right Secretariat for two months he contested and refuted twenty-four matters in all; those who deliberated feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Right Secretariat for two months he contested and refuted twenty-four matters in all; those who deliberated feared him.

sentences.zh: 復為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again made Vice-Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Vice-Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，詔求直言。

translations.literal: A comet appeared; an edict sought frank speech.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared; an edict sought frank speech.

sentences.zh: 敦復奏：「昔康澄以『賢士藏匿，四民遷業，上下相徇，廉恥道消，毀譽亂真，直言不聞』為深可畏。

translations.literal: Yan Dunfu memorialized: "In the past Kang Cheng held that 'worthy men in hiding, the four classes shifting occupations, superiors and subordinates covering for one another, the way of integrity and shame exhausted, slander and praise confounding truth, and straight counsel going unheard' were deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Dunfu submitted a memorial: "Kang Cheng once warned that when worthy men withdraw into hiding, the four orders of society abandon their proper trades, officials shield one another from top to bottom, shame and integrity fade away, reputation drowns out truth, and honest counsel never reaches the throne—the state is in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗即其言考已然之事，多本于左右近習及姦邪以巧佞轉移人主之意。

translations.literal: Your servant has tested his words against what has already happened, and the pattern for the most part originates with those close at hand in attendance and with wicked men who, through sly flattery, divert the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed his words against events already past, and I find that the root cause lies with court intimates and corrupt officials who, through artful flattery, turn the emperor's mind from its proper course.

sentences.zh: 其惡直醜正，則能使賢士藏匿；

translations.literal: When they hate the upright and revile the correct, they can make worthy men hide away;
translations.idiomatic: When they despise integrity and malign the righteous, worthy men are driven into seclusion;

sentences.zh: 其造為事端，則能使四民遷業；

translations.literal: when they manufacture incidents, they can make the four classes shift occupations;
translations.idiomatic: when they manufacture crises, the people abandon their proper livelihoods;

sentences.zh: 其委曲彌縫，則能使上下相徇；

translations.literal: when they weave excuses and patch over faults, they can make superiors and subordinates cover for one another;
translations.idiomatic: when they smooth over wrongdoing with evasions, officials at every level shield one another;

sentences.zh: 其假寵竊權，簧鼓流俗，則能使廉恥道消；

translations.literal: when they borrow favor and usurp authority, drumming on the reed pipe to sway the vulgar, they can make the way of integrity and shame exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: when they exploit imperial favor to seize power and inflame public opinion, the nation's sense of shame is extinguished;

sentences.zh: 其誣人功罪，則能使毀譽亂真；

translations.literal: when they falsify men's merits and crimes, they can make slander and praise confound truth;
translations.idiomatic: when they distort men's deeds and punishments, reputation replaces truth;

sentences.zh: 其壅蔽聰明，則能使直言不聞。

translations.literal: when they block and obscure clear hearing, they can make straight counsel go unheard.
translations.idiomatic: when they seal off the emperor's ears, honest counsel never reaches the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣願防微杜漸，以助應天之實。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to guard against the subtle and stop the gradual, to help fulfill the substance of responding to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that we guard against small evils before they grow, so that our response to Heaven's warning may be genuine."

sentences.zh: 又論：「比來百司不肯任責，瑣屑皆取決朝省，事有不當，上煩天聽者，例多取旨。

translations.literal: He further argued: "Recently the hundred offices have been unwilling to bear responsibility; trivial matters all await decision from the court and province, and when affairs are improper and the Son of Heaven's hearing is troubled, the usual practice is to seek the sovereign's instruction.
