translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Lately every ministry has shirked its duties. Petty matters are all referred upward to the central court, and whenever something goes wrong the emperor must be consulted for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 由是宰執所治煩雜，不減有司，天子聽覽，每及細務，非所以為政。

translations.literal: Because of this the chief ministers' business is as vexing and complex as that of the regular offices, and whenever the Son of Heaven listens and reads he reaches down to minute affairs—this is not the way to govern.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that the chief ministers are as burdened as the line officials, and the emperor is drawn into trivial detail at every turn. That is no way to govern a state.

sentences.zh: 願詳其大，略其細。」

translations.literal: I wish to examine the great and set aside the small."
translations.idiomatic: Let the throne attend to great matters and leave the small ones to those charged with them."

sentences.zh: 八年，金遣使來要以難行之禮，詔侍從，臺諫條奏所宜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Jin sent envoys to demand observance of rites difficult to carry out; the edict ordered the attendants and the censorial remonstrators to memorialize on what was appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the reign, Jin dispatched envoys insisting on humiliating ceremonial terms. The emperor ordered his attendants and censorial officials to submit recommendations on how to respond.

sentences.zh: 敦復言：「金兩遣使，直許講和，非畏我而然，安知其非誘我也。

translations.literal: Dunfu said: "The Jin twice sent envoys and straightway permitted peace talks—not because they feared us, but how do we know they are not luring us?
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu argued: "Jin has twice sent envoys offering peace—not out of fear of us. Who is to say they are not baiting a trap?

sentences.zh: 且謂之屈己，則一事既屈，必以他事來屈我。

translations.literal: Moreover, if we call it humbling ourselves, then once one matter is humbled, they will surely use some other matter to humble us.
translations.idiomatic: And if we call this "humbling ourselves," one concession will only invite the next.

sentences.zh: 今所遣使以詔諭為名，儻欲陛下易服拜受，又欲分廷抗禮，還可從乎？

translations.literal: Now the envoys sent come in the name of imperial proclamation—if they wish Your Majesty to change dress and bow to receive it, and also wish to divide the court and receive them with equal ceremony, can we still follow?
translations.idiomatic: These envoys come bearing an "imperial proclamation." Suppose they demand that Your Majesty change into ceremonial dress and bow to receive it, or that they be received with equal standing in the hall—could we agree even to one such demand?

sentences.zh: 苟從其一二，則此後可以號令我，小有違異，即成釁端，社稷存亡，皆在其掌握矣。」

translations.literal: If we follow them in one or two points, then thereafter they can command us by signal; the slightest deviation will become a pretext for rupture, and the preservation or destruction of the altars of soil and grain will all lie in their grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Yield on one or two points and they will soon be issuing commands to us. The smallest breach of protocol will become a casus belli, and the fate of the dynasty will rest entirely in their hands."

sentences.zh: 時秦檜方力贊屈己之說，外議群起，計雖定而未敢行。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui was vigorously advocating the policy of humbling oneself; outside opinion rose in a body, and though the plan was settled they still did not dare carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was then vigorously promoting the policy of national humiliation. Public outrage was widespread, and even after a decision was taken the court still hesitated to act on it.

sentences.zh: 勾龍如淵說檜，宜擇人為臺官，使擊去異論，則事遂矣。

translations.literal: Gou Long Ruyuan advised Qin Hui that he should select men for censorial posts to drive away dissenting opinion, and then the matter would be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Long Ruyuan urged Qin Hui to place his own men in the censorate and purge dissenting voices—then the policy could proceed unopposed.

sentences.zh: 於是如淵、施廷臣、莫將皆據要地，人皆駭愕。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruyuan, Shi Tingchen, and Mo Jiang all occupied important posts, and everyone was struck with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyuan, Shi Tingchen, and Mo Jiang were accordingly installed in key positions, to the shock of the court.

sentences.zh: 敦復同尚書張燾上疏言：「前日如淵以附會和議得中丞，今施廷臣又以此躋橫榻，眾論沸騰，方且切齒，莫將又以此擢右史。

translations.literal: Dunfu together with the Minister of Works Zhang Tao submitted a memorial saying: "Earlier Ruyuan, by attaching himself to the peace agreement, obtained the post of vice censor-in-chief; now Shi Tingchen has by the same means ascended to the privy bench. Public discussion boils over and teeth are set on edge, and now Mo Jiang has by this been promoted to right recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu and Minister of Works Zhang Tao jointly memorialized: "Ruyuan won the vice censorate by endorsing the peace terms; now Shi Tingchen has used the same route to a seat on the privy council. The court is in an uproar, and Mo Jiang has just been promoted to right recorder by the same means.

sentences.zh: 夫如淵、廷臣庸人，但知觀望，將則姦人也，陛下奈何與此輩斷國論乎？

translations.literal: Ruyuan and Tingchen are mediocre men who know only how to watch which way the wind blows; Mo Jiang is a wicked man—why does Your Majesty discuss the fate of the state with such as these?
translations.idiomatic: Ruyuan and Tingchen are mediocrities who watch which way the wind blows; Mo Jiang is an outright villain. Why does Your Majesty entrust the nation's policy to men like these?

sentences.zh: 乞加斥逐，杜群枉門，力為自治自強之策。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be further expelled and driven away, that the gate of factional wrong be closed, and that effort be made for policies of self-governance and self-strengthening."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that they be dismissed and driven from office, that the door to factional corruption be shut, and that the court commit itself to genuine self-governance and self-strengthening."

sentences.zh: 既又與燾等同班入對，爭之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again entered audience together with Tao and the others and disputed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Tao then appeared before the throne together with their colleagues and argued the point at length.

sentences.zh: 檜使所親諭敦復曰：「公能曲從，兩地旦夕可至。」

translations.literal: Qin Hui had someone close to him instruct Dunfu, saying: "If you, sir, can bend to follow, the two capitals can be recovered within days."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui sent an intermediary to tell Dunfu: "If you will only yield on this point, both capitals can be recovered within days."

sentences.zh: 敦復曰：「吾終不為身計誤國家，況吾薑桂之性，到老愈辣，請勿言。」

translations.literal: Dunfu said: "I will never for the sake of my person err and harm the state; moreover my nature is like ginger and cassia—the older I grow the sharper I become. Please say no more."
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu replied: "I will never sacrifice the state for my own advancement—and my disposition is like ginger and cassia bark: the older I grow, the sharper I become. Say no more."

sentences.zh: 檜卒不能屈。

translations.literal: Qin Hui in the end could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui could not break him.

sentences.zh: 胡銓謫昭州，臨安遣人械送貶所。

translations.literal: Hu Quan was demoted to Zhaozhou; Lin'an dispatched men to send him in fetters to his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quan was banished to Zhaozhou, and the Lin'an authorities sent men to escort him to exile in chains.

sentences.zh: 敦復往見守臣張澄曰：「銓論宰相，天下共知，祖宗時以言事被謫，為開封者必不如是。」

translations.literal: Dunfu went to see the guarding official Zhang Cheng and said: "Quan criticized the chief minister—a fact known throughout the realm. In the time of our ancestors, when men were demoted for speaking out, those who received them at Kaifeng never acted thus."
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu went to the local prefect Zhang Cheng and said: "Everyone knows Hu Quan was punished for criticizing the chief minister. In former reigns, officials exiled for remonstrance were never treated this way at Kaifeng."

sentences.zh: 澄愧謝，為追還。

translations.literal: Cheng, ashamed, apologized and had him recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng, ashamed, apologized and had the chains removed.

sentences.zh: 始檜拜相，制下，朝士相賀，敦復獨有憂色曰：「姦人相矣。」

translations.literal: When Qin Hui first received appointment as chief minister and the appointment edict was issued, court gentlemen congratulated one another; Dunfu alone wore a look of worry and said: "A wicked man is chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui was first appointed chief minister and the edict was promulgated, the court congratulated itself—Dunfu alone looked troubled and said: "A villain holds the chief ministership."

sentences.zh: 張致遠、魏矼聞之，皆以其言為過。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyuan and Wei Kang heard this and both regarded his words as excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan and Wei Kang both thought he had gone too far.

sentences.zh: 至是竄銓，敦復謂人曰：「頃言秦之姦，諸君不以為然，今方專國便敢爾，他日何所不至耶？」

translations.literal: When Quan was now banished, Dunfu said to others: "Earlier when I spoke of Qin's wickedness you gentlemen did not agree; now that he monopolizes the state he dares act thus—what will he not do hereafter?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Quan was banished, Dunfu told others: "When I warned that Qin was a villain, none of you believed me. Now that he controls the state outright, he dares do this—what limit will there be tomorrow?"

sentences.zh: 權吏部尚書兼江淮等路經制使。

translations.literal: He was appointed provisional Minister of Personnel and concurrently Commissioner for the Huai and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Minister of Personnel and concurrently commissioner for the Huai River region and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 故事，侍從過宰相閣，既退，宰相必送數步。

translations.literal: By precedent, when attendants passed the chief minister's pavilion and had withdrawn, the chief minister always saw them off several paces.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a palace attendant passed the chief minister's office on leaving audience, the minister always walked him out several paces.

sentences.zh: 敦復見檜未嘗送，每曰：「人必自侮而後人侮之。」

translations.literal: When Dunfu saw Qin Hui he was never seen off, and each time Dunfu said: "A man must first demean himself before others demean him."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui never walked Dunfu out. Each time Dunfu remarked: "A man must first demean himself before others will demean him."

sentences.zh: 尋請外，以寶文閣直學士知衢州，提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: Before long he requested an outside post and was made academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Quzhou, with charge of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested a provincial appointment and was made academician of the Baowen Pavilion, prefect of Quzhou, and superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 閒居數年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: Living in retirement several years, he died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in retirement he died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 敦復靜默如不能言，立朝論事無所避。

translations.literal: Dunfu was silent as though unable to speak, yet when he stood at court and discussed affairs he avoided nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu was quiet and unassuming, as though he could scarcely speak at all—yet once at court on official business he held back nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂之曰：「卿鯁峭敢言，可謂無忝爾祖矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to him: "You are stern and bold in speech and may be said not to have disgraced your ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him: "You are blunt and fearless in remonstrance. You have not disgraced your forebears."

sentences.zh: 黃龜年

translations.literal: Huang Guinian
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guinian

sentences.zh: 黃龜年，字德邵，福州永福人。

translations.literal: Huang Guinian, styled Deshao, was a man of Yongfu in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guinian, styled Deshao, was a native of Yongfu in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧五年進士第，調洺州司理參軍，累官河北西路提舉學士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning and was appointed judicial assistant in Luozhou; he rose through offices to become academician for the Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning, was appointed judicial assistant in Luozhou, and rose through successive posts to academician for the Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩見而奇之，入為太常博士。

translations.literal: Lü Yihao saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, and brought him in as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao was struck by his talent and brought him to court as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，除吏部員外郎，拜監察御史，尋除尚書左司員外郎、中書門下檢正房公事，充修政局檢討官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and commissioned as investigating censor; soon after he was made vice director in the Left Section of the Department of State Affairs, charged with rectifier duties in the Secretariat-Chancellery rectification office, and served as review officer of the Reform Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and commissioned as investigating censor; soon after he was made vice director in the Left Section of the Department of State Affairs, charged with rectifier duties in the Secretariat-Chancellery rectification office, and served as review officer of the Reform Bureau.

sentences.zh: 乞令檢正官察通進司，帝從其請。

translations.literal: He requested that rectification officers oversee the Communication Office; the Emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that rectification officers oversee the Communication Office, and the Emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 時頤浩再相，植黨傾秦檜，引朱勝非奉京祠兼侍讀，恐中書舍人胡安國持錄黃不下，特命龜年書行，議者譏其侵官。

translations.literal: At the time Yihao was chancellor again, his faction worked to displace Qin Hui. He brought in Zhu Shengnon for capital temple service concurrent with lecturing, fearing Secretariat Drafting Officer Hu Anguo would withhold the recorded yellow, and specially ordered Guinian to sign and execute the appointment; critics ridiculed this as overstepping office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lü Yihao was chancellor again, his faction worked to displace Qin Hui. He brought in Zhu Shengnon for capital temple service concurrent with lecturing, fearing Secretariat Drafting Officer Hu Anguo would withhold the recorded yellow, and specially ordered Guinian to sign and execute the appointment; critics ridiculed this as overstepping office.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 會邊報王倫來歸，龜年劾檜專主和議，沮止恢復，植黨專權，漸不可長。

translations.literal: When border reports came that Wang Lun had returned, Guinian impeached Qin Hui for monopolizing the peace policy, obstructing recovery, planting a faction and monopolizing power—gradually this could not be allowed to continue.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier reports announced Wang Lun's return from Jin, Guinian impeached Qin Hui for monopolizing the peace policy, blocking recovery of lost territory, building a faction, and concentrating power—a trend that could not be allowed to continue.

sentences.zh: 乃上書曰：「臣聞一言而盡事君之道曰忠，罪莫大於欺君；

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that one word exhausts the way of serving one's ruler—it is loyalty; no crime is greater than deceiving one's ruler;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "One word sums up service to one's ruler: loyalty. No crime is greater than deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 一言而盡輔政之道曰公，罪莫大於私己。

translations.literal: one word exhausts the way of assisting in government—it is public-mindedness; no crime is greater than serving oneself.
translations.idiomatic: One word sums up assisting in government: public-mindedness. No crime is greater than serving oneself.

sentences.zh: 臣人者背公而徇私，則刑賞僭濫。

translations.literal: When ministers turn their backs on the public and follow private ends, rewards and punishments become presumptuous and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: When officials pursue private ends against the public good, rewards and punishments are applied arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 慮人主之照其姦，則合黨締交，相與比周，熒惑主聽。

translations.literal: Fearing that the ruler will see through their wickedness, they form factions and bind alliances, assisting one another in comparison and encirclement, and bewildering the ruler's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, they form cliques, bind one another in alliance, and cloud the emperor's judgment.

sentences.zh: 故附下罔上之黨盛，而威福之柄下移，禍有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: Thus the faction that attaches below and deceives above flourishes, and the handle of authority and favor shifts downward; the disaster is beyond what words can express.
translations.idiomatic: The faction that deceives the throne from below grows strong, power slips from the emperor's hands, and the consequences are beyond words.

sentences.zh: 伏見秦檜還自金國，陛下驟任，不一年而超至宰輔，乃不顧國家，盜威福在己，欲永塞言路。」

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully observes that Qin Hui, returning from the Jin state, was suddenly entrusted by Your Majesty and within less than a year was promoted straight to chief minister; then he cared nothing for the state, stole authority and favor to himself, and wished forever to block the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Qin Hui, on returning from Jin, was suddenly elevated by Your Majesty and within a year reached the chief ministership. He then cared nothing for the state, seized power for himself, and sought permanently to silence all criticism."

sentences.zh: 書上，檜罷，並劾檜黨王㬇、王昞、王守道，皆罷之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Qin Hui was dismissed, and he also impeached Qin's faction Wang Biao, Wang Bing, and Wang Shoudao—all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Qin Hui was dismissed, and Guinian also impeached Qin's allies Wang Biao, Wang Bing, and Wang Shoudao—all were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 檜乃授觀文殿大學士、提舉江州太平觀，官如故。

translations.literal: Qin Hui was then granted the Grandee of the Hall for Viewing Culture and charge of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou, his rank remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was granted the title Grandee of the Hall for Viewing Culture and made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou, retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 龜年又奏：「比論檜徇私欺君，合正典刑，投諸裔土，以禦魑魅。

translations.literal: Guinian again memorialized: "Recently in impeaching Qin Hui for serving himself and deceiving the ruler, he should have been punished according to the canonical penalty and cast to the distant borderlands to guard against evil spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian memorialized again: "Qin Hui deserved canonical punishment for deceiving the throne and serving himself—exile to the frontier to ward off evil.

sentences.zh: 今乃任便居住，雖陛下曲全大臣之禮，秦檜姦狀暴露，復寵以儒學最上職名，俾優遊琳館，聽其自如。

translations.literal: Now he is allowed to reside where he wishes; although Your Majesty in bending to the full rites due great ministers shows forbearance, Qin Hui's wicked conduct is exposed, yet he is again favored with the highest scholarly title and permitted to live at ease in a fine hall, listening as he pleases.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he has been allowed to live where he chooses. Your Majesty has shown the forbearance due a great minister—but Qin Hui's crimes are exposed, and he has been rewarded with the highest scholarly title and permitted to live in comfort at a palace abbey.

sentences.zh: 律斷群盜，必分首從，為之從者皆已伏誅，獨置渠魁可乎？」

translations.literal: The law in judging bandit gangs must distinguish ringleaders from followers; those who followed have already been executed—can the chief alone be left untouched?"
translations.idiomatic: The law distinguishes ringleaders from followers in bandit cases. The followers have already been punished—can the ringleader alone go free?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣聞恩莫隆于父子，義莫重於君臣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant has heard that no favor surpasses that between father and son, and no righteousness surpasses that between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "No bond is holier than that between father and son; no duty is weightier than that between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 不義則後其君，不仁則遺其親。

translations.literal: Without righteousness one puts one's ruler last; without benevolence one abandons one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Without righteousness a man ranks his ruler last; without benevolence he abandons his kin.

sentences.zh: 君親既然，則何忌憚而不為。

translations.literal: Once ruler and kin are thus treated, what is there to fear and not do?
translations.idiomatic: Once a man has betrayed ruler and kin, what will he not dare to do?

sentences.zh: 檜厚貌深情，矯言偽行，進迫君臣之勢，陽為面從；

translations.literal: Qin Hui has a thick appearance and deep feelings, speaks falsely and acts deceptively; advancing he presses the situation between ruler and minister and outwardly feigns compliance;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui wears a mask of virtue while harboring deep deceit. To the emperor's face he feigns compliance while pressing his advantage in the ruler-minister relationship;

sentences.zh: 退恃朋比之姦，陰謀沮格。

translations.literal: retreating he relies on the wickedness of factional comparison, secretly plotting obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: behind the throne he relies on his faction to obstruct policy in secret.

sentences.zh: 上不畏陛下，中不畏大臣，下不畏天下之議，無忌憚如此。

translations.literal: Above he does not fear Your Majesty, in the middle he does not fear great ministers, below he does not fear discussion throughout the realm—he is without fear and restraint to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He fears neither the emperor above, nor the great ministers around him, nor public opinion below. His audacity knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 欺君私己，有一即可黜，況檜之欺與私顯著者為多乎？」

translations.literal: Deceiving the ruler and serving oneself—one such offense suffices for dismissal; how much more when Qin Hui's deceit and self-serving are conspicuous and numerous?"
translations.idiomatic: Deceiving the throne or serving oneself—either alone warrants dismissal. Qin Hui's deceit and self-interest are flagrant and manifold."

sentences.zh: 章凡三上，遂褫檜職。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted three times in all, and Qin Hui's office was then stripped.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted three times in succession, and Qin Hui was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 復上章曰：「檜行詭而言譎，外縮而中邪，以巧詐取相位，姦回竊國柄，收召險佞，蟠結黨與。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "Qin Hui's conduct is devious and his words crafty; outwardly he shrinks back while inwardly he is perverse; by cunning fraud he seized the post of chief minister, by wickedness and rebellion he stole the handle of state, gathered in the dangerous and flatterers, and coiled into factions.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "Qin Hui's conduct is devious and his words treacherous; outwardly submissive, inwardly corrupt. By cunning he seized the chief ministership, by treachery he usurped state power, gathered sycophants and dangerous men, and built a faction.

sentences.zh: 陛下以智臨而辨之早，以剛決而去之速，故端人正士，舉手相慶，蓋以公天下之同惡耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with wisdom presiding and discerning early, with firm resolution removing him swiftly—thus upright men throughout the court raised their hands in mutual rejoicing, for the most part because the realm shared the same hatred of evil.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, discerning early and acting decisively, has removed him—and upright men throughout the court rejoice, for the realm shares this hatred of evil.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下發明詔，以檜潛慝隱惡暴白於天下，使知陛下數易相位真不得已也；

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to issue a clarifying edict, exposing Qin Hui's hidden wickedness and concealed evil to the realm, so that all may know Your Majesty's repeated changes of chief minister were truly unavoidable;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty issue a clarifying edict exposing Qin Hui's hidden crimes to the realm, so that all may understand why the throne has changed chief ministers so often—

sentences.zh: 又所以破為臣姦膽，庶朋比之風不復作矣。」

translations.literal: this also serves to break the wicked courage of ministers; perhaps the wind of factional comparison will not arise again."
translations.idiomatic: and so that the wicked may be deterred and the wind of factional collusion may not rise again."

sentences.zh: 除太常少卿，累遷起居舍人、中書舍人兼給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and successively promoted to diarist, drafting secretary, and concurrently supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was successively promoted to diarist, drafting secretary, and supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 侍御史常同言龜年陰結大臣，致身要地，又交結諸將，趣操不正，罷歸。

translations.literal: Supervising censor Chang Tong said Guinian had secretly bound himself to great ministers to reach an important post, and also associated with various generals; his conduct and purpose were not upright, and he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Chang Tong accused Guinian of cultivating ties with senior ministers to advance himself and of associating with military commanders—conduct unworthy of his office. He was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 司諫詹大方希檜意劾龜年附麗匪人，搢紳不齒，落職，本貫居住。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Zhan Dafang, seeking to please Qin Hui, impeached Guinian for attaching himself to unworthy men; the gentry would not rank him with themselves; his office was removed and he was made to reside in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Zhan Dafang, currying favor with Qin Hui, impeached Guinian for associating with unworthy men. The gentry would have nothing to do with the charge, but Guinian was stripped of office and confined to his native district.

sentences.zh: 卒，六十三。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 龜年微時，永福簿李朝旌奇之，許妻以女。

translations.literal: When Guinian was young, Li Chaojing, registrar of Yongfu, regarded him as extraordinary and promised him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, Li Chaojing, registrar of Yongfu, recognized his talent and promised him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 龜年既登第，而朝旌已死，家貧甚。

translations.literal: After Guinian passed the examination, Chaojing had already died and the family was extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Guinian passed the jinshi examination, Chaojing had died and the family was destitute.

sentences.zh: 或勸龜年別娶，龜年正色曰：「吾許以諾，死而負之，何以自立。」

translations.literal: Some urged Guinian to marry elsewhere; Guinian said with stern countenance: "I gave my word; if I fail him in death, how can I stand upright?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to marry elsewhere. Guinian said firmly: "I gave my word. If I abandon it now that he is dead, how can I face myself?"

sentences.zh: 遂娶之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he married her.
translations.idiomatic: He married her.

sentences.zh: 任子恩，先奏其弟之子，人皆義之。

translations.literal: When exercising the privilege of appointing a son by merit, he first nominated his younger brother's son; all regarded this as righteous.
translations.idiomatic: When exercising the privilege of appointing a kinsman by merit, he nominated his younger brother's son first—an act everyone praised as righteous.

sentences.zh: 子衡，仕至湖南提舉。

translations.literal: His son Heng rose to become fiscal intendant of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng rose to the post of fiscal intendant of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 程瑀，字伯㝢，饒州浮梁人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu, styled Boyu, was a man of Fuliang in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, styled Boyu, was a native of Fuliang in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 其姑臧氏婦，養瑀為子，姑沒，始復本姓。

translations.literal: His aunt, a woman of the Zang clan, and her husband raised Yu as their son; when the aunt died he then resumed his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: His aunt of the Zang clan and her husband raised him as their own; when she died he resumed his original surname.

sentences.zh: 少有聲太學，試為第一，累官至校書郎。

translations.literal: In youth he had renown in the Imperial Academy; in examination he ranked first and he rose through offices to collator.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was renowned in the Imperial Academy, ranked first in examination, and rose to the post of collator.

sentences.zh: 為臧氏父母服，服闋，除兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for the Zang clan's parents; when mourning ended he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning for his foster parents of the Zang clan; when the mourning period ended he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 適高麗使回，充送伴使。

translations.literal: When the Goryeo envoy was returning, he was appointed escort commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When a Goryeo envoy was returning home, he was appointed escort commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，使者往返江、浙間，調挽舟夫甚擾，有詔禁止。

translations.literal: Previously, when envoys traveled back and forth between the Yangzi and Zhe regions, requisitioning boat haulers had caused great disturbance; an edict forbade this.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, envoys traveling between the Yangzi and Zhe regions had caused great hardship by requisitioning boat haulers; an edict now forbade the practice.

sentences.zh: 提舉人舡王珣畫別敕，遇風逆水澁許調夫。

translations.literal: The commissioner for imperial vessels Wang Xun drafted a separate edict permitting requisition of haulers when wind was adverse and the current obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun, commissioner for imperial vessels, drafted a supplementary edict permitting hauler requisition when wind and current were adverse.

sentences.zh: 瑀渡淮，見民丁挽舟如故，遂劾珣，珣反奏瑀違御筆。

translations.literal: When Yu crossed the Huai he saw commoners hauling boats as before; he thereupon impeached Xun, and Xun in turn memorialized that Yu had violated the emperor's brush edict.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Huai, Yu saw commoners still hauling boats as before. He impeached Wang Xun, who counter-memorialized that Yu had violated the emperor's personal edict.

sentences.zh: 詔命淮南提舉潘良貴核實，良貴奏珣言非是。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Pan Lianggui, fiscal intendant of Huainan, to verify the facts; Lianggui memorialized that Xun's statement was not correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Pan Lianggui, fiscal intendant of Huainan, to investigate. Lianggui reported that Wang Xun's account was false.

sentences.zh: 金人入侵，求可使者，瑀請往。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded, the court sought an envoy; Yu volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded, the court sought an envoy, and Yu volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 未行，會欽宗即位，議割三鎮，命瑀往河東，秦檜往河中。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Qinzong acceded to the throne. As the court debated ceding the three prefectures, Yu was ordered to Hedong and Qin Hui to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Qinzong acceded to the throne. As the court debated ceding the three prefectures, Yu was sent to Hedong and Qin Hui to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 瑀奏：「臣願奉使，不願割地。」

translations.literal: Yu memorialized: "Your servant wishes to go as envoy but does not wish to cede territory."
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized: "Your servant wishes to go as envoy but does not wish to cede territory."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: His memorial went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 至中山，諸將已得密諭，城守不下。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhongshan, the generals had already received secret orders and held the city without surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhongshan, the generals had already received secret orders and refused to surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 瑀與金使王汭俱至燕山。

translations.literal: Yu and the Jin envoy Wang Ni both proceeded to the Yan Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the Jin envoy Wang Ni both proceeded to the Yan Mountains.

sentences.zh: 還，除左正言，即言股肱大臣莫肯以身任天下事，且論：「欲慕祖宗而遹追無術，欲斥奄宦而寵任益堅，欲鋤姦惡而薄示典刑，欲汰濫繆而苟容僥倖，兼聽而不能行其言，委任而不能責其效，苟且之習復成，黨與之私浸廣，最時病之大者。」

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Left Rectifier and at once said that the great ministers serving as the emperor's arms and legs would not personally shoulder affairs of state. He argued: "One wishes to emulate the ancestors yet has no means to pursue them earnestly; one wishes to drive out eunuch officials yet favors and employs them ever more steadfastly; one wishes to uproot wickedness yet only lightly displays punishments; one wishes to purge extravagance and error yet tolerates undeserved favor; one listens broadly yet cannot act on what is said, delegates responsibility yet cannot demand results—shabby expedients are revived, partisan private interests spread ever wider: these are the greatest ills of the age."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Left Rectifier and at once said that the great ministers would not personally shoulder affairs of state. He argued: "One wishes to emulate the ancestors yet has no means to pursue them earnestly; one wishes to drive out eunuch officials yet favors them ever more; one wishes to uproot wickedness yet only lightly punishes it; one wishes to purge extravagance and error yet tolerates undeserved favor; one listens broadly yet cannot act on what is said, delegates responsibility yet cannot demand results—shabby expedients are revived and partisan private interests spread ever wider. These are the greatest ills of the age."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕非不知此，慮有未盡，決意行之有失耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am not unaware of this; I worry that matters are not yet fully considered and that if I resolve firmly to act there will be faults."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I am not unaware of this; I worry that matters are not yet fully considered and that if I resolve firmly to act there will be faults."

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「事固當熟慮，然優柔不斷，實隳事功。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Matters indeed should be deliberated thoroughly, yet prolonged indecision in truth undermines achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Matters indeed should be deliberated thoroughly, yet prolonged indecision in truth undermines achievement."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「李綱宣撫兩路，外議謂何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "Li Gang is pacification commissioner for both routes—what does public opinion say?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "Li Gang is pacification commissioner for both routes—what does public opinion say?"

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「僉論固以為宜。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Public opinion indeed considers it appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Public opinion indeed considers it appropriate.

sentences.zh: 然綱前與大臣議論不合，須賴聖明照察其心，任之無疑可也。」

translations.literal: Yet Gang previously disagreed with chief ministers in debate; one must rely on Your Sacred Sagacity to discern his heart and appoint him without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gang previously disagreed with chief ministers in debate; one must rely on Your Sacred Sagacity to discern his heart and appoint him without doubt."

sentences.zh: 金酋斡離不、粘罕爭功，故斡離不欲和，粘罕欲戰，朝廷遣人齎蠟書約余睹，皆為粘罕所得。

translations.literal: The Jin chieftains Wanyan Zonghan and Wanyan Nianhan contended for merit; therefore Zonghan did not wish for peace while Nianhan wished to fight. The court sent men bearing wax-sealed letters to treat with Yelü Yende—all were captured by Nianhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin commanders Wanyan Zonghan and Wanyan Nianhan were rivals for credit: Zonghan opposed peace while Nianhan favored war. The court sent envoys with sealed letters to negotiate with Yelü Yende—all were intercepted by Nianhan.

sentences.zh: 瑀因言：「金兵圍我重鎮，數月不能解，豈能出塞共謀人之國。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon said: "The Jin army has besieged our key strongholds for months without being able to break them—how can they go beyond the frontier to plot against another state?
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued: "The Jin army has besieged our strongholds for months without success—how can they spare forces to plot against another kingdom?

sentences.zh: 莫若遣使議和，然謹飭邊備，徐觀其變。」

translations.literal: Better to send an envoy to discuss peace, yet carefully order frontier defenses and slowly observe their changes."
translations.idiomatic: Better to send an envoy to discuss peace, but tighten frontier defenses and watch how matters develop."

sentences.zh: 使未行。

translations.literal: The envoy had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy had not yet been dispatched.

sentences.zh: 瑀復言：「徐處仁庸俗，吳敏昏懦，唐恪傾險，政事所以不振。

translations.literal: Yu again said: "Xu Churen is vulgar, Wu Min is muddle-headed, and Tang Ke is overbearing and dangerous—the reason government affairs do not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Yu added: "Xu Churen is a mediocrity, Wu Min is a fool, and Tang Ke is treacherous and overbearing—that is why government is in disarray.

sentences.zh: 請盡黜免，別選英賢，共圖大計。」

translations.literal: I ask that they all be dismissed and replaced, and that other worthy and able men be selected to plan the great strategy together."
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss them all and appoint worthy men to chart the nation's course."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the proposal and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 時御史李光言星變，帝疑以問瑀，對言：「陛下毋問有無，第正事修德，則變異可消。」

translations.literal: At the time supervising censor Li Guang spoke of a change in the stars; the emperor, doubtful, asked Yu, who replied: "Your Majesty need not ask whether there is one or not; simply rectify affairs and cultivate virtue, and the anomaly can be dispelled."
translations.idiomatic: When supervising censor Li Guang reported celestial anomalies, the emperor asked Yu for his view. Yu replied: "Your Majesty need not ask whether the omen is real. Rectify governance and cultivate virtue, and the portent will pass."

sentences.zh: 瑀嘗論蔡京罪，帝因言吳敏庇京，又疑光黨京，謂瑀曰：「須卿作文字來。」

translations.literal: Yu once argued the crimes of Cai Jing; the emperor then spoke of Wu Min shielding Jing and also suspected Guang of being in Jing's faction, saying to Yu: "I need you, sir, to write a document on this."
translations.idiomatic: Yu once argued for punishing Cai Jing. The emperor mentioned Wu Min's protection of Jing and suspected Li Guang of belonging to Jing's faction, telling Yu: "I need you to draft a memorial on this."

sentences.zh: 瑀辭。

translations.literal: Yu declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined.

sentences.zh: 改屯田郎官，謫瑀監漳州鹽稅。

translations.literal: He was changed to an official in the Directorate of Agriculture and Yu was demoted to superintendent of the salt tax in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Directorate of Agriculture, then demoted to superintendent of the salt tax in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，召為司封員外郎，遷光祿少卿、國子司業。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Yu was summoned as vice director in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Yu was summoned as vice director in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 請祠，主管亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: He requested a temple post and was put in charge of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a temple appointment and was made superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋召赴行在，疏十事以獻。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the mobile court and submitted a memorial of ten items.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the mobile court and presented a memorial outlining ten policy recommendations.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣、提點江東刑獄，召為太常少卿，遷給事中兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was appointed direct access to the Secretariat, fiscal judicial intendant for Jiangdong, summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to supervising censor concurrently lecturing attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed with direct access to the Secretariat, made fiscal judicial intendant for Jiangdong, summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to supervising censor and lecturing attendant.

sentences.zh: 建修政局，其目曰省費裕國、強兵息民。

translations.literal: He established a policy of renovation; its headings were economizing expenditure to enrich the state and strengthening the army to give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a program of reform under two headings: cutting expenditure to enrich the treasury, and building military strength to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 瑀條上十四事，皆切時務。

translations.literal: Yu itemized and submitted fourteen matters, all pressing on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted fourteen specific proposals, each addressing an urgent problem of the day.

sentences.zh: 時三衙單弱，五軍多出於盜，瑀言：「李捧、崔增輩各將其徒，張俊、王𤫉本無兵機，今呂頤浩出征，即捧、增輩便可使隸戎行。」

translations.literal: At the time the Three Commands were weak and the Five Armies were largely drawn from bandits; Yu said: "Li Peng, Cui Zeng, and their like each command their followers; Zhang Jun and Wang Si originally had no military expertise—now that Lü Yihao is campaigning in the field, Peng, Zeng, and their like can straightway be made to serve in the army."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Commands were understrength and the Five Armies were largely recruited from bandits. Yu argued: "Men like Li Peng and Cui Zeng already command their own followers. Zhang Jun and Wang Si have no real military experience—yet with Lü Yihao in the field, Peng and Zeng could be pressed into service immediately."

sentences.zh: 帝因言：「頤浩熟於軍事，在外總諸將，檜在朝廷，庶幾內外相應，然檜誠實，但太執耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor then said: "Yihao is skilled in military affairs; outside he commands the generals, and Hui is at court—perhaps inside and outside can respond to each other; yet Hui is honest, only too stubborn."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Yihao knows warfare. With him commanding the armies in the field and Hui at court, the civil and military branches should work in concert. Hui is honest—only rather inflexible."

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「如求機警能順旨者，極不難得，但不誠實，則終不可倚。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "If you seek men who are quick-witted and able to follow the sovereign's intent, they are extremely easy to obtain—but if they are not honest, in the end they cannot be relied upon."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Clever men who know how to read the emperor's wishes are easy to find. But without honesty, none of them can be trusted."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 權邦彥除簽書樞密院，瑀言邦彥五罪，疏三上，不報。

translations.literal: Quan Bangyan was appointed co-signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yu listed five crimes of Bangyan and submitted memorials three times without response.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Bangyan was appointed co-signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Yu charged him with five crimes and submitted three memorials—all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 求罷，除兵部侍郎，不拜，以敷文閣待制知信州。

translations.literal: He requested dismissal and was appointed vice minister of war; he did not accept and was made reader of the Fuwen Pavilion and prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved and was appointed vice minister of war, but declined the post and was made reader of the Fuwen Pavilion and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 待御史江公躋左司諫方公孟，言瑀不可去，復以為給事中。

translations.literal: Awaiting censor Jiang Gongji and left remonstrance official Fang Gongmeng said Yu must not be removed and he was again made supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiang Gongji and left remonstrance official Fang Gongmeng argued that Yu must not be dismissed, and he was restored as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 久之，復命知信州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again ordered to serve as prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was again ordered to serve as prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 胡安國、劉一止言：「瑀忠信可以備獻納，正直可以司風憲，不宜去。」

translations.literal: Hu Anguo and Liu Yizhi said: "Yu's loyalty and trustworthiness qualify him for presenting remonstrance; his uprightness qualifies him to oversee censorial discipline—he should not be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo and Liu Yizhi argued: "Yu's loyalty and integrity make him fit to remonstrate at court; his uprightness makes him fit to uphold censorial standards. He should not be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 遂復留。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again retained.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly kept at court.

sentences.zh: 頤浩薦席益，既得旨，以御批示後省官。

translations.literal: Yihao recommended Xi Yi; once the imperial decision was obtained, he showed the imperial endorsement to the rear secretariat officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao recommended Xi Yi; once the emperor's approval was obtained, he circulated the imperial endorsement among the secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「益為人公豈不知，何必用？」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Everyone knows what kind of man Yi is—why must he be used?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu objected: "Everyone knows what Xi Yi is like. Why appoint him at all?"

sentences.zh: 頤浩曰：「給事不見御批耶？」

translations.literal: Yihao said: "Supervising censor, did you not see the imperial endorsement?"
translations.idiomatic: Yihao retorted: "Did you not see the emperor's endorsement?"

sentences.zh: 瑀曰：「已見矣。

translations.literal: Yu said: "I have already seen it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied: "I saw it.

sentences.zh: 公不能執奏，乃先示瑀輩，欲使不敢論駁耶？

translations.literal: You, sir, could not memorialize in opposition, yet first showed it to Yu and his colleagues—did you wish to make us dare not dispute and refute?
translations.idiomatic: You could not memorialize in opposition yourself, so you showed it to us first—was that meant to silence our objections?

sentences.zh: 然益之來，非公福也。」

translations.literal: Yet Yi's coming will not be your good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: But Xi Yi's appointment will bring you no good fortune."

sentences.zh: 頤浩赧然，即劾益。

translations.literal: Yihao flushed and immediately impeached Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao flushed with embarrassment and immediately impeached Xi Yi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以言者罷，提舉亳州明道宮，尋復徽猷閣待制、知撫州，無何，提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Before long, on the words of critics he was dismissed, put in charge of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou; before long he was again made reader of the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Fuzhou; shortly thereafter he was put in charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, critics brought about his dismissal and he was made superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou. He was soon restored as reader of the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Fuzhou, then shortly afterward made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 居父母喪，服除，知嚴州，徙宣州，復奉祠。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his parents; when mourning ended he was prefect of Yanzhou, transferred to Xuanzhou, and again granted a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his parents, he served as prefect of Yanzhou, was transferred to Xuanzhou, and again granted a temple appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄召赴行在，除兵部侍郎兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed vice minister of war concurrently reading attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the mobile court and appointed vice minister of war and reading attendant.

sentences.zh: 因論：「鄧禹嘗言『興衰在德厚薄，初不論大小』。

translations.literal: In discussion he said: "Deng Yu once said, 'Rise and fall depend on the thickness of virtue and do not at first depend on size.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he cited Deng Yu: "A dynasty's rise or fall depends on the depth of its virtue—not on the size of its territory.

sentences.zh: 光武不數年定大業，禹言如合符契。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu within a few years settled the great enterprise; Yu's words matched as though by tally.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu secured the empire within a few years, exactly as Deng Yu had predicted.

sentences.zh: 今英俊滿朝，豈無為陛下畫至計者，願厲志而已。」

translations.literal: Now talented men fill the court—is there no one to draw the supreme plan for Your Majesty? I wish only that Your Majesty steel your will."
translations.idiomatic: Talented men fill the court today. Surely someone can chart the path to recovery—Your Majesty has only to summon the will."

sentences.zh: 尋遷翊善。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 論：「金人入侵，未嘗一大衄，有輕我心，豈可保其不背盟。

translations.literal: He argued: "The Jin people invaded and never suffered a major defeat; they hold our strength in contempt—how can we guarantee they will not break the treaty?
translations.idiomatic: He warned: "The Jin have invaded repeatedly without suffering a major defeat. They hold us in contempt. How can we trust them to keep the peace?

sentences.zh: 宜省費抑末，常賦外一毫不取於民，民日益厚，兵日益強，使金人不敢窺為長計。」

translations.literal: One should economize expenditure and restrain secondary occupations; beyond the regular tax not a single hair should be taken from the people—the people daily grow richer and the army daily grows stronger, so that the Jin people dare not look on this as a long-term plan."
translations.idiomatic: Cut spending and curb luxury trades. Beyond the regular tax, take not a penny more from the people. As the people grow wealthier and the army stronger, Jin will not dare treat us as a permanent inferior."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「且作十年。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Let us plan for ten years."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Let us plan for ten years."

sentences.zh: 瑀再拜曰：「十年之說，願陛下早夜毋忘。」

translations.literal: Yu bowed again and said: "On the plan of ten years, I wish Your Majesty never to forget it morning and night."
translations.idiomatic: Yu bowed and said: "Then let Your Majesty never forget this ten-year plan, morning or night."

sentences.zh: 除兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 檜既主和，瑀議論不專以和為是，檜忌之，改龍圖閣學士、知信州。

translations.literal: When Hui had taken charge of peace, Yu in discussion did not exclusively regard peace as correct; Hui resented him and had him changed to academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qin Hui committed the court to peace, Yu refused to treat peace as the only option. Qin Hui resented him and had him transferred to academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 會大水，檜見瑀奏牘，謂同列曰：「堯之洪水，不至如是。」

translations.literal: When a great flood occurred, Hui saw Yu's memorial and said to his colleagues: "The flood of Yao did not reach this degree."
translations.idiomatic: During a great flood, Qin Hui read Yu's memorial and told his colleagues: "Even the flood of Emperor Yao was not this bad."

sentences.zh: 瑀遂稱疾，提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon pleaded illness and was put in charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pleaded illness and was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐通書李光，降朝議大夫，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Convicted of corresponding with Li Guang, he was demoted to Grandee of Court Discussion; he died at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of corresponding with the disgraced Li Guang, he was demoted to Grandee of Court Discussion. He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 瑀在朝無詭隨，嘗為《論語說》，至「弋不射宿」，言孔子不欲陰中人。

translations.literal: Yu at court was without evasive compliance; he once wrote Explanations of the Analects, and at "the archer does not shoot at roosting birds" he said Confucius did not wish to strike men from hiding.
translations.idiomatic: At court Yu never trimmed his words to please. In his Explanations of the Analects, on the passage "the archer does not shoot a bird at rest," he wrote that Confucius meant one should not strike an enemy from ambush.

sentences.zh: 至「周公謂魯公」，則曰可為流涕。

translations.literal: At "the Duke of Zhou spoke to the Duke of Lu" he said one could weep for it.
translations.idiomatic: On "the Duke of Zhou addressed the Duke of Lu," he wrote that the passage could move one to tears.

sentences.zh: 洪興祖序述其意，檜以為譏己，逐興祖。

translations.literal: Hong Xingzu in his preface set forth this meaning; Hui regarded it as satire of himself and drove Xingzu away.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xingzu's preface to the work elaborated this reading. Qin Hui took it as a personal attack and had Hong Xingzu banished.

sentences.zh: 魏安行鋟版京西漕司，亦奪安行官，籍其家，毀版。

translations.literal: Wei Anxing printed an edition for the Western Capital transport commission; Hui also stripped Anxing of office, confiscated his household, and destroyed the blocks.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anxing printed an edition through the Western Capital transport office. Qin Hui stripped him of office, confiscated his property, and destroyed the printing blocks.

sentences.zh: 檜死，瑀子孫乃免錮云。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Yu's descendants were then released from restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Qin Hui's death were Yu's descendants released from official restriction.

sentences.zh: 有奏議六卷。

translations.literal: He left six fascicles of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He left six fascicles of submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 張闡字大猷，永嘉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chan, styled Dayou, was a man of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan, styled Dayou, was a native of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 幼力學，博涉經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: From youth he studied hard, broadly mastered the classics and histories, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied diligently, mastered the classics and histories, and wrote with distinction.

sentences.zh: 將命名，夢神人大書「闡」字曰：「以是名爾。」

translations.literal: When he was about to be named, he dreamed that a divine man wrote large the character "Chan" and said: "With this name you."
translations.idiomatic: Before he was named, his father dreamed that a divine figure wrote the character chan in large script and said: "Name him thus."

sentences.zh: 父異之，力勉其為學。

translations.literal: His father regarded this as strange and vigorously urged him to study.
translations.idiomatic: His father took this as an omen and pressed him to devote himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 未冠，由舍選貢京師。

translations.literal: Before reaching capped age he was selected from the academy and sent as tribute to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he was selected from the local academy and sent to the capital as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 登宣和六年進士第，調嚴州兵曹掾兼治右獄。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Xuanhe and was appointed military adjutant of Yanzhou, concurrently overseeing the right prison.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Xuanhe and was appointed military adjutant of Yanzhou, with concurrent charge of the right prison.

sentences.zh: 時方臘作亂，闡倡守禦計。

translations.literal: At the time Fang La was in rebellion; Chan advocated a plan of defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rebelled, Zhang Chan proposed a defensive strategy.

sentences.zh: 有義士請身督戰，既戰，稍卻，州將怒，付闡治，將殺之，闡力爭曰：「是士以義請戰，官軍卻，勢不得獨前，非首奔者，殺之何罪？」

translations.literal: A volunteer asked to lead the battle in person; after battle they were slightly repulsed; the prefect was angry, handed him to Chan for judgment, and was about to execute him; Chan forcefully disputed, saying: "This man asked to fight out of righteousness; the official army retreated—he could not advance alone; he was not the first to flee—what crime is there in killing him?"
translations.idiomatic: A volunteer had offered to lead the attack in person. When the battle went poorly and government troops fell back, the prefect was furious and handed the man to Zhang Chan for punishment, intending to execute him. Zhang Chan protested vigorously: "This man volunteered out of loyalty. The army retreated—he could not advance alone. He was not the first to flee. What crime warrants death?"

sentences.zh: 州將意解，士得免。

translations.literal: The prefect's intent was resolved and the man was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect relented and the man was spared.

sentences.zh: 李回帥江西，席益帥湖南，皆辟置幕下。

translations.literal: Li Hui commanded Jiangxi and Xi Yi commanded Hunan; both recruited him to their staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, military commissioner of Jiangxi, and Xi Yi, military commissioner of Hunan, both recruited him to their staffs.

sentences.zh: 群盜據洞庭，官軍多西北人，不閑水戰。

translations.literal: Bandit gangs occupied Dongting; the official army was largely men of the northwest and unskilled in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits held Dongting Lake, and the government troops—mostly northerners—were unskilled in naval combat.

sentences.zh: 闡建策造戰艦，以大艦為營，小艦出戰，乘水涸直搗賊巢，賊勢以衰。

translations.literal: Chan proposed building warships, using large ships as camps and small ships for battle; taking advantage of low water he struck straight at the bandits' nest and the bandits' strength thereby declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan proposed building warships: large vessels as floating camps, small ones for attack. When the water fell he led a direct assault on the bandit stronghold and broke their power.

sentences.zh: 諸司交薦，改秩，吏部以微文沮之，闡弗辯，求嶽祠歸。

translations.literal: Various offices jointly recommended him for promotion; the Ministry of Personnel blocked it with petty regulations; Chan did not dispute and requested a mountain abbey post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Multiple offices recommended him for promotion, but the Ministry of Personnel blocked it on procedural grounds. Zhang Chan did not protest and requested a mountain abbey appointment, then returned home.

sentences.zh: 歷鄂、台二州教授。

translations.literal: He served as instructor in E and Tai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as instructor in Ezhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興十年，詔侍從各舉所知，給事中林待聘以闡聞，召對。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shaoxing an edict ordered each palace attendant to recommend someone known to him; supervising censor Lin Daipin reported Chan and he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Shaoxing the emperor ordered each palace attendant to recommend a worthy man. Supervising censor Lin Daipin nominated Zhang Chan, who was summoned for audience.

sentences.zh: 時金人議和，歸關中地。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin people were discussing peace and returning the Guanzhong territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was then negotiating peace and offering to return the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 闡首言：「關中必爭之地，古號天府，願固守以蔽巴蜀，圖中原。」

translations.literal: Chan spoke first: "Guanzhong is territory that must be contested; anciently it was called the Storehouse of Heaven—I wish to hold it firmly to shield Ba and Shu and plan for the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan spoke first: "Guanzhong is contested ground—the ancient Storehouse of Heaven. We must hold it firmly to shield Sichuan and plan recovery of the north."

sentences.zh: 次言監司、郡守薦舉之弊。

translations.literal: Next he spoke of the abuses in recommendations by surveillance commissioners and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He then addressed abuses in the recommendation system for surveillance commissioners and prefects.

sentences.zh: 又乞嚴禁遏糴，以濟江、浙水患。

translations.literal: He also asked that hoarding and purchase of grain be strictly forbidden, to relieve the water disaster in Jiang and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged strict prohibition of grain hoarding to relieve the flood disaster in Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，除秘書省正字，遷校書郎兼吳、益王府教授。

translations.literal: He was summoned to examination for a library post, appointed corrector of the Secretariat, and promoted to collator concurrently instructor to the princes of Wu and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination, was appointed corrector of the Secretariat, and promoted to collator and instructor to the princes of Wu and Yi.

sentences.zh: 時諸將恃功邀爵賞，有過則姑息，又兵布於外，禁衛單寡，闡上疏極論之。

translations.literal: At the time the generals relied on merit to demand enfeoffment and reward; when they had faults they were treated with indulgence; moreover troops were deployed outside while the palace guard was thin and few; Chan submitted a memorial arguing this to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Generals then traded on their victories to demand titles and rewards, while their failures went unpunished; troops were scattered in the provinces while the palace guard was dangerously thin. Zhang Chan submitted a forceful memorial on all these points.

sentences.zh: 後稍進退諸將必當其實，且召諸道兵以益禁旅，皆如闡言。

translations.literal: Later when generals were gradually promoted or demoted it always matched the facts, and when troops from various circuits were summoned to augment the palace guard—all accorded with Chan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently, when generals were promoted or demoted, the decisions matched their actual merit; and when provincial troops were recalled to strengthen the palace guard—the court followed Zhang Chan's advice.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷秘書郎兼國史院檢討官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to secretary concurrently reviser of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to secretary and reviser of the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 秦檜每薦臺諫，必先諭以己意，嘗謂闡曰：「秘書久次，欲以臺中相處何如？」

translations.literal: Each time Qin Hui recommended censorial remonstrators he first instructed them in his own intent; he once said to Chan: "You have long been at the Secretariat—how would it be to place you in the censorate?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Qin Hui recommended censorial officials he first told them what he expected. He once asked Zhang Chan: "You have served long in the Secretariat—would you like a post in the censorate?"

sentences.zh: 闡謝曰：「丞相見知，得老死秘書幸矣！」

translations.literal: Chan declined, saying: "If the chief minister knows me, to die old in the Secretariat would be fortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan declined: "If the chief minister knows my worth, let me end my days in the Secretariat—that would be fortune enough!"

sentences.zh: 檜默然，竟罷，主管台州崇道觀，歷泉、衢二州通判。

translations.literal: Hui was silent and in the end dismissed him; he was put in charge of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou and served as administrative vice prefect of Quan and Qu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui said nothing further and eventually had him dismissed. Zhang Chan was made superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou and served as vice prefect of Quanzhou and Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十五年冬，帝躬攬萬機，起闡提舉兩浙路市舶，入為御史臺檢法官，升吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, winter, the emperor personally took hold of all affairs of state and recalled Chan to supervise the Two-Zhe maritime trade office; he entered court as examining judge of the Censorate and was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-fifth year the emperor resumed personal governance and recalled Zhang Chan to supervise maritime trade in the Two-Zhe region. He entered court as examining judge of the Censorate and was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 孝宗在王邸，帝妙選宮僚，謂「莊重老成無逾闡者」，改命祠部兼建王府贊讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong was at the princely residence the emperor finely selected palace staff and said: "None surpasses Chan for dignity, solidity, and maturity," and changed the appointment to the Ministry of Rites concurrently reader for the Jian Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Xiaozong was still prince, the emperor chose his household staff with care and said: "No one is more steady and seasoned than Zhang Chan," appointing him to the Ministry of Rites as reader for the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春，大雨，無麥苗，荊、浙盜起，詔侍從、臺諫條陳弭災、禦盜之術。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-first year great rain fell and there were no wheat seedlings; bandits arose in Jing and Zhe; an edict ordered palace attendants and censorial remonstrators to memorialize on methods of quelling disaster and repelling bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-first year torrential rains destroyed the wheat crop and bandits rose in Hubei and Zhejiang. The emperor ordered attendants and censorial officials to submit plans for disaster relief and bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 闡上疏曰：「和議以來，歲有聘幣，民不堪命，臣願陛下毋以金人困中國可乎？

translations.literal: Chan submitted a memorial saying: "Since the peace agreement there have been annual tribute missions and the people cannot bear the burden—I wish Your Majesty not to regard the Jin people's draining of China as acceptable, can you?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan memorialized: "Since the peace treaty we have paid tribute every year until the people can bear no more. Will Your Majesty stop treating Jin's drain on China as acceptable?

sentences.zh: 歸正人時有遣還之命，怨聲聞道路，臣願陛下毋使金人得以甘心可乎？

translations.literal: When surrendered northerners are sometimes ordered sent back, the sound of resentment is heard on the roads—I wish Your Majesty not to let the Jin people have their satisfaction, can you?
translations.idiomatic: When surrendered northerners are sent back against their will, the roads echo with their grief. Will Your Majesty stop giving Jin that satisfaction?

sentences.zh: 州縣吏職卑地遠，漁奪之禍被於編籍，臣願陛下嚴髒吏之誅可乎？

translations.literal: County and prefectural officials hold low rank and distant posts; the disaster of plunder and seizure falls on the registered population—I wish Your Majesty to strictly punish corrupt officials, can you?
translations.idiomatic: County and prefectural officials are poorly paid and far from oversight—they prey on the people. Will Your Majesty punish corrupt local officials severely?

sentences.zh: 蠲租之令，已赦復征，寬大之澤例為虛文，臣願陛下申詔令之禁可乎？

translations.literal: Edicts remitting rent, once pardoned are again collected; the grace of leniency routinely becomes empty words—I wish Your Majesty to enforce the prohibition of edicts and orders, can you?
translations.idiomatic: Rent remissions granted in edicts are collected again once the amnesty expires—imperial grace becomes empty words. Will Your Majesty enforce the spirit of those edicts?

sentences.zh: 是數者能次第行之，則足以動天地，召和氣，災異、盜賊不足慮也。」

translations.literal: If these several matters can be carried out in sequence, then it suffices to move Heaven and Earth, summon harmonious qi, and disaster anomalies and bandits need not be worried over."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will act on these points in turn, Heaven itself will respond, harmony will return, and neither disaster nor banditry need trouble us further."

sentences.zh: 又言：「金主亮將入侵，宜守要害，防海道，三邊不可無良將，督視不可無大帥。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Jin ruler Hailing is about to invade; one should hold key positions, guard the sea routes, leave no frontier without a good general, and leave no grand campaign without a supreme commander."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Jin ruler Hailing is preparing to invade. We must hold the strategic passes, guard the coast, station able generals on every frontier, and appoint a supreme commander for the overall campaign."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝嘉納，面諭曰：「卿所言深中時病，但遣人北歸，已載約書，朕不忍渝也。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor praised and accepted it and addressed him face to face, saying: "What you, sir, have said deeply hits the illness of the times—but sending men north in return is already written in the treaty, and I cannot bear to violate it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial and told Zhang Chan in person: "Your analysis cuts to the heart of our problems—but repatriating northerners is already written into the treaty, and I cannot bring myself to break it."

sentences.zh: 遷將作監，進宗正少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of palace construction and advanced to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of palace construction and vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，孝宗即位，闡權工部侍郎兼侍講，入謝，言：「諸將以敗為捷，冒受爵秩，州廂禁軍因覃霈皷譟，希厚賞，不可不正其罪。」

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, when Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Chan was provisional vice minister of works concurrently lecturing attendant; entering to give thanks he said: "The generals report defeat as victory and presumptuously receive enfeoffment and rank; in the prefectural barracks the forbidden army, on receiving a general amnesty, clamored and made a disturbance, hoping for generous reward—their crimes must be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, when Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Zhang Chan was appointed acting vice minister of works and lecturing attendant. In his audience of thanks he said: "Generals report defeats as victories and receive titles they do not deserve. Garrison troops riot at every amnesty, demanding rewards they have not earned. These crimes must be punished."

sentences.zh: 時悉為施行。

translations.literal: At the time all were carried out as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The court acted on every point.

sentences.zh: 金主亮死，葛王褒復求和，再議遣使。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Hailing died, Prince Ge Wang Bao again sought peace and again they deliberated sending envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin ruler Hailing was assassinated, Prince Ge (the future Emperor Shizong) renewed peace overtures and the court again debated sending envoys.

sentences.zh: 闡言：「宜嚴遣使之命，正敵國之禮，彼或不從，則有戰爾。

translations.literal: Chan said: "One should strictly order the mission of the envoys and correct the ceremonial of equal states; if they do not follow, then there is only war.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan argued: "Send envoys with strict instructions and insist on proper diplomatic ceremony. If Jin refuses, we fight—that is all.

sentences.zh: 如是，則中國之威可以復振。」

translations.literal: If it is thus, then the prestige of China can again be revived."
translations.idiomatic: Only then can China's standing be restored."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「使者報聘，故事也，舊約不從，朕志定矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Envoys returning courtesy calls are precedent; if the old agreement is not followed, my resolve is fixed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Courtesy missions are established practice. If Jin will not honor the old terms, my mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 是冬，給劄侍從、臺諫條具時務，闡上十事皆剴切。

translations.literal: That winter, an edict was issued for attendants and censorial remonstrators to itemize current affairs; Chan submitted ten items, all incisive.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor ordered attendants and censorial officials to submit policy recommendations. Zhang Chan offered ten proposals, each sharply argued.

sentences.zh: 當時應詔數十人，惟闡與國子司業王十朋指陳時事，斥權幸，無所回隱。

translations.literal: At the time several tens of men responded to the edict; only Chan and vice director of the Directorate of Education Wang Shipeng pointed out current affairs and reproached the powerful, without any evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens responded to the edict, but only Zhang Chan and Wang Shipeng, vice director of the Directorate of Education, spoke plainly about current affairs and condemned the powerful without evasion.

sentences.zh: 明日，召兩人對內殿，帝大加稱賞，賜酒及御書。

translations.literal: The next day the two men were summoned to the inner hall; the emperor greatly praised them and bestowed wine and imperial writing.
translations.idiomatic: The next day both were summoned to the inner hall. The emperor praised them warmly and bestowed wine and a scroll in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 時進太上皇帝、太上皇后冊寶，工部例進官，闡辭。

translations.literal: At the time when presenting the seals and regalia of the Retired Emperor and Retired Empress, the Ministry of Works by precedent advanced in rank; Chan declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the seals and regalia of the Retired Emperor and Retired Empress were presented, the Ministry of Works by custom received a promotion. Zhang Chan declined.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「公轉一階，則澤可以及子孫，奈保辭？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "If you, sir, advance one rank, then the grace can reach your descendants—why preserve your declination?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "Accept one rank and the benefit passes to your descendants. Why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 闡笑曰：「寶冊非吾功也，吾能為子孫冒無功賞乎？」

translations.literal: Chan smiled and said: "The seals and regalia are not my achievement—can I for my descendants presume on reward without merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan smiled: "The regalia ceremony was not my doing. How could I accept unearned reward for my descendants?"

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，真拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he was truly appointed vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he was formally appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 闡奏：「臣去冬乞守禦兩淮，陛下謂春首行之，夏秋當畢，今其時矣。」

translations.literal: Chan memorialized: "Your servant last winter asked to defend the Two Huai; Your Majesty said it would be done at the start of spring and completed by summer and autumn—now the time has come."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan memorialized: "Last winter I asked to oversee defense of the Two Huai. Your Majesty said spring would be the start and the work would be finished by summer or autumn. That time has come."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「江、淮事盡付張浚，朕倚浚為長城。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Affairs of the Jiang and Huai are entirely entrusted to Zhang Jun—I rely on Jun as my Great Wall."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Matters on the Jiang and Huai are entirely in Zhang Jun's hands. I rely on him as my Great Wall."

sentences.zh: 會督府請受蕭琦降，詔問闡，闡請受其降。

translations.literal: When the supreme command requested acceptance of Xiao Qi's surrender, the edict asked Chan; Chan asked to accept the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the supreme command requested permission to accept Xiao Qi's surrender, the emperor consulted Zhang Chan, who advised accepting it.

sentences.zh: 俄報王師收復靈壁縣，闡慮大將李顯忠、邵宏淵深入無援，奏請益兵殿后。

translations.literal: Before long it was reported that the imperial army had recovered Lingbi County; Chan feared that the great generals Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan, advancing deep without support, memorialized asking to increase troops to cover the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the imperial army had retaken Lingbi County. Zhang Chan, fearing that Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan had advanced too deep without support, memorialized for reinforcements to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 已而王師果失利，眾論歸罪於戰。

translations.literal: Before long the imperial army indeed met defeat; public discussion blamed the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The army was indeed defeated, and public opinion blamed the campaign.

sentences.zh: 闡曰：「陛下出師受降是也。

translations.literal: Chan said: "Your Majesty's dispatch of the army to accept surrender was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan said: "Your Majesty was right to send the army to accept the surrender.

sentences.zh: 諸將違節度且無援而敗，當矯前失，安可遽沮銳氣。」

translations.literal: The generals violated command discipline and were defeated for lack of reinforcements; one should correct the earlier mistake—how can we suddenly dampen fighting spirit?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals broke command and were defeated without reinforcements—we should remedy that earlier error, not abruptly crush the army's fighting spirit."

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，益出御前器甲付諸軍，手詔勞浚，軍聲復振。

translations.literal: The Emperor was impressed by his words and issued more armor and weapons from the imperial stores to the armies; he personally wrote an edict encouraging Zhang Jun, and army morale revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was stirred by his argument and released more armor and weapons from the imperial armory to the troops, sending a personal edict to encourage Zhang Jun until army morale rallied again.

sentences.zh: 時數易臺諫，闡力言之，請增廣諫員。

translations.literal: At the time the remonstrating officials at the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau were frequently changed; Chan spoke forcefully and requested that their numbers be increased.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrating officials at the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau were being replaced again and again; Chan argued forcefully that their ranks should be expanded.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「臺諫好名，如某人但欲得直聲而去。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Those at the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau love reputation—for example, so-and-so merely wanted a reputation for bluntness and then left.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The censors and remonstrators love their reputations—take so-and-so, who only wanted to be known for blunt speech and then left."

sentences.zh: 闡曰：「唐德宗疑姜公輔為賣直，陸贄切諫，願陛下深以為鑒。」

translations.literal: Chan said: 'Emperor Dezong of Tang suspected Jiang Gongfu of selling bluntness; Lu Zhi remonstrated sharply. Your Majesty, I hope you will take this deeply to heart as a warning.'
translations.idiomatic: Chan replied, "Emperor Dezong of Tang suspected Jiang Gongfu of 'selling bluntness,' and Lu Zhi remonstrated with force—I beg Your Majesty to take that as a solemn warning."

sentences.zh: 帝再三嘉獎。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and rewarded him again and again.

sentences.zh: 金人求和，帝與闡議，闡曰：「彼欲和，畏我耶？

translations.literal: When the Jurchens sought peace, the Emperor discussed it with Chan. Chan said: 'They want peace—do they fear us?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens asked for peace, the Emperor consulted Chan, who said, "They want peace—do they fear us?

sentences.zh: 愛我耶？

translations.literal: Do they love us?
translations.idiomatic: Do they love us?

sentences.zh: 直款我耳。」

translations.literal: They are simply trying to win us over with smooth words.'
translations.idiomatic: They are simply trying to win us over with smooth words."

sentences.zh: 力陳六害不可許。

translations.literal: He forcefully set forth six harms and argued that peace must not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully laid out six harms and argued that peace must not be granted.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕意亦然，姑隨宜應之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'My thinking is the same; for now let us respond as circumstances require.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I agree—but for the moment let us answer as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 帝記「賣直」之語，謂：「胡銓亦及此。

translations.literal: The Emperor remembered the remark about 'selling bluntness' and said: 'Hu Quan also speaks this way.
