translations.idiomatic: The Emperor remembered the talk of "selling bluntness" and said, "Hu Quan speaks the same way.

sentences.zh: 朕非拒諫者，辨是非耳。」

translations.literal: I am not one who rejects remonstrance—I simply distinguish right from wrong.'
translations.idiomatic: I am not one who rejects remonstrance—I simply distinguish right from wrong."

sentences.zh: 闡曰：「聖度當如天，奈何與臣下爭名。」

translations.literal: Chan said: 'Your Majesty's magnanimity should be like Heaven—why compete with your subjects for reputation?'
translations.idiomatic: Chan said, "Your Majesty's magnanimity should be like Heaven—why contend with your ministers for a name?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'What you say is right.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 頃之，除工部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 金副元帥紇石烈志寧以書諭通好，所請三事，國書、歲幣之議已定，惟割唐、鄧、海、泗未決，將遣王之望、龍大淵通問，而眾言紛紛不已。

translations.literal: Jin vice commander-in-chief He Shilie Zhining sent a letter proposing friendly relations. Of the three matters requested, the terms regarding the state letter and annual tribute had been settled; only the cession of Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si prefectures remained unresolved. The court was about to dispatch Wang Zhiwang and Long Dayuan to negotiate, yet popular opinion remained clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin vice commander-in-chief He Shilie Zhining sent a letter proposing friendly relations. Of the three matters at issue, terms for the state letter and annual tribute were settled; only the cession of Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si prefectures remained in dispute. The court was about to send Wang Zhiwang and Long Dayuan to negotiate, yet public debate would not cease.

sentences.zh: 闡謂：「不與四州乃可通和，議論先定乃可遣使，今彼為客，我為主，我以仁義撫天下，彼以殘酷虐吾民，觀金勢已衰，何必先示以弱。」

translations.literal: Chan said: 'Only if we do not cede the four prefectures can peace be pursued; only if policy is settled first can envoys be sent. Now they are the guest and we the host. We govern the realm with benevolence and righteousness; they cruelly oppress our people. Seeing that Jin power is already waning, why show weakness first?'
translations.idiomatic: Chan said, "Peace is possible only if we refuse the four prefectures; envoys can be sent only after policy is settled. They are the guest and we the host—we rule the realm with benevolence and righteousness while they cruelly abuse our people. Jin power is already fading; why show weakness first?"

sentences.zh: 朝論韙之。

translations.literal: Court opinion approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion approved.

sentences.zh: 帝用真宗故事，命經筵官二員遞宿學士院，以備顧問，闡入對尤數。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhenzong's precedent, the Emperor ordered two members of the Classics Mat lecturers to take turns lodging in the Hanlin Academy to be available for consultation; Chan was summoned for audience especially often.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Zhenzong's precedent, the Emperor ordered two Classics Mat lecturers to lodge in turn at the Hanlin Academy for consultation; Chan was summoned to audience with especial frequency.

sentences.zh: 屢引疾乞骸骨，帝不忍其去。

translations.literal: He repeatedly cited illness to request retirement; the Emperor could not bear to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pleaded illness to retire, and the Emperor could not bear to let him leave.

sentences.zh: 二年，闡請益力，乃除顯謨直學士、提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of his tenure, Chan asked with greater insistence, and was then appointed Direct Academic of the Exalted Policies Hall and Director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Chan pressed harder still and was finally made Direct Academic of the Exalted Policies Hall and Director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝問所欲言，闡奏：「許和則忘祖宗之仇，棄四州則失中原之心，遣歸正人則傷忠義之氣。

translations.literal: At his audience to take leave, the Emperor asked what he wished to say. Chan memorialized: 'If we agree to peace, we forget the enmity owed our ancestors; if we abandon the four prefectures, we lose the hearts of the Central Plains; if we send back those who have defected to us, we wound the spirit of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the Emperor asked what he wished to say. Chan memorialized, "If we accept peace, we forget our ancestral enmity; if we abandon the four prefectures, we lose the heart of the Central Plains; if we send back loyalists who have come over to us, we break the spirit of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下毋忘老臣平昔之言。」

translations.literal: I only hope Your Majesty will not forget what your aged subject said in former days.'
translations.idiomatic: I only ask that Your Majesty not forget what your old servant said in former days."

sentences.zh: 其指時事尤諄切，帝眷益篤。

translations.literal: His allusions to current affairs were especially earnest; the Emperor's regard for him grew deeper still.
translations.idiomatic: His remarks on current affairs were especially urgent and sincere, and the Emperor's regard for him deepened.

sentences.zh: 諭以秋涼復召，加賜金犀帶，特許佩魚。

translations.literal: He instructed him to return when the autumn turned cool, granted him a gold and rhinoceros-horn belt in addition, and specially permitted him to wear the fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him to return when autumn cooled, added a gold and rhinoceros-horn belt to his gifts, and specially allowed him to wear the fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 居家逾月卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: After more than a month at home he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month at home he died, at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 特贈端明殿學士。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the title of Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 朱熹嘗言：「秦檜挾敵要君，力主和議，群言勃勃不平。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi once said: 'Qin Hui, wielding the enemy to hold the ruler hostage, forcefully advocated peace talks, and voices of protest seethed everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi once said, "Qin Hui, wielding the enemy to hold the throne hostage, forcefully pushed peace talks while voices of protest seethed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 檜既摧折忠臣義士之氣，遂使士大夫懷安成習。

translations.literal: Once Qin had crushed the spirit of loyal ministers and righteous men, he made the literati take ease as habit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qin had broken the spirit of loyal ministers and righteous men, he made the literati settle into complacency.

sentences.zh: 至癸未和議，則知其非者鮮矣。

translations.literal: By the peace agreement of the guimao year, few still knew it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: By the guimao peace agreement, few still knew it was wrong.

sentences.zh: 朝論間有建白，率雜言利害，其言金人世仇不可和者，惟胡右史銓、張尚書闡耳。」

translations.literal: When court opinion occasionally offered proposals, they mostly mixed talk of profit and loss. Of those who said the Jurchens were an ancestral enemy with whom peace was impossible, only Right Clerk Hu Quan and Minister Zhang Chan.'
translations.idiomatic: When court opinion did speak up, it mostly mixed talk of profit and loss. Of those who said the Jurchens were an ancestral foe with whom peace was impossible, only Right Clerk Hu Quan and Minister Zhang Chan."

sentences.zh: 子叔椿。

translations.literal: His son was Shu Chun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shu Chun.

sentences.zh: 洪擬，字成季，一字逸叟，鎮江丹陽人。

translations.literal: Hong Ni, courtesy name Chengji, also styled Yisou, was a native of Danyang in Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Ni, courtesy name Chengji and also styled Yisou, was from Danyang in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 本弘姓，其先有名璆者，嘗為中書令，避南唐諱，改今姓。

translations.literal: His original surname was Hong; an ancestor named You had once served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and, to avoid a taboo of Southern Tang, changed to the present surname.
translations.idiomatic: The family surname had originally been Hong; an ancestor named You had once served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and, to avoid a Southern Tang taboo, changed to the present surname.

sentences.zh: 後復避宣祖廟諱。

translations.literal: Later they again avoided the taboo name of the Founding Ancestor's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later they again avoided the taboo of the Founding Ancestor's temple name.

sentences.zh: 遂因之。

translations.literal: They followed that practice thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the change thereafter.

sentences.zh: 擬登進士甲科。

translations.literal: Ni passed the jinshi examination in the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ni passed the jinshi examination in the top tier.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中為國子博士，出提舉利州路學事，尋改福建路。

translations.literal: During the Chongning era he served as Doctor of the National University, then went out as Director of Educational Affairs for Lizhou Circuit, and soon transferred to Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era he was Doctor of the National University, then went out as Director of Educational Affairs for Lizhou Circuit and soon transferred to Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐譴，通判鄆州，復提舉京西北路學事，歷湖南、河北東路。

translations.literal: Suffering demotion, he was made Vice-Prefect of Yanzhou; later he again directed educational affairs for the Northwest Capital Circuit, and served in Hunan and Hebei East circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After demotion he served as Vice-Prefect of Yanzhou, then again directed educational affairs for the Northwest Capital Circuit and held posts in Hunan and Hebei East circuits.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，為監察御史，遷殿中，進侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era he was Remonstrance Official, then promoted to Palace Remonstrance Official and then Court Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe era he was Remonstrance Official, then Palace Remonstrance Official, then Court Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 時王黼、蔡京更用事，擬中立無所附會。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Fu and Cai Jing alternated in power; Ni stood neutral and attached himself to neither faction.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu and Cai Jing were alternating in power; Ni stood apart and joined neither faction.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史許景衡罷，擬亦坐送吏部，知桂陽軍，改海州。

translations.literal: When Palace Remonstrance Official Xu Jingheng was dismissed, Ni was also sent to the Ministry of Personnel because of the affair; he was made Military Prefect of Guiyang, then transferred to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Remonstrance Official Xu Jingheng was dismissed, Ni was sent to the Ministry of Personnel in the same affair, made Military Prefect of Guiyang, and later transferred to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 時山東盜起，屢攻城，擬率兵民堅守。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in Shandong and repeatedly attacked cities; Ni led soldiers and civilians in a firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising in Shandong and repeatedly assaulting cities; Ni led soldiers and civilians in a resolute defense.

sentences.zh: 建炎間，居母憂，以秘書少監召，不起。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era, while mourning his mother, he was summoned as Vice-Director of the Secretariat but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era, while in mourning for his mother, he was summoned as Vice-Director of the Secretariat but declined.

sentences.zh: 終喪，為起居郎、中書舍人，言：「兵興累年，饋餉悉出於民，無屋而責屋稅，無丁而責丁稅，不時之須，無名之斂，殆無虛日，所以去而為盜。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Attendant of the Secretariat and Drafting Drafter of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and said: 'War has continued for years; supplies all come from the people. Houses are taxed though they have no roof; men are taxed though they have no adult sons. Untimely demands and nameless levies scarcely cease for a day—this is why people leave and become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became Attendant of the Secretariat and Drafting Drafter of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and said, "War has dragged on for years and every supply comes from the people. They are taxed for houses though they have no roof, taxed for adult sons though they have none. Untimely demands and nameless levies scarcely pause for a day—this is why people flee and turn bandit.

sentences.zh: 今關中之盜不可急，宜求所以弭之，江西之盜不可緩，宜求所以滅之。

translations.literal: Now the bandits in Guanzhong must not be pressed too hard; one should seek means to pacify them. The bandits in Jiangxi must not be handled too leniently; one should seek means to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits in Guanzhong must not be pressed too hard—find means to pacify them. The bandits in Jiangxi must not be handled too gently—find means to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 夫豐財者政事之本，而節用者又豐財之本也。」

translations.literal: Enriching the treasury is the foundation of good government, and frugality is in turn the foundation of enrichment.'
translations.idiomatic: Enriching the treasury is the root of good government, and frugality is the root of enrichment."

sentences.zh: 高宗如越，執政議移蹕饒、信間，擬上疏力爭，謂「舍四通五達而趨偏方下邑，不足以示形勢、固守禦。」

translations.literal: When Gaozong went to Yue, the chief councillors discussed moving the imperial residence to the region between Rao and Xin. Ni submitted a memorial arguing forcefully that 'to abandon a place where four roads meet and five roads run, and rush toward a remote small town, is insufficient to display our strategic posture or provide a firm defense.'
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong went to Yue, the chief councillors discussed moving the court to the region between Rao and Xin. Ni submitted a forceful memorial arguing that "to abandon a place where four roads meet and five roads cross, and flee to a remote small town, is not enough to show our strategic position or hold a firm defense."

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、吏部尚書，言者以擬未嘗歷州縣，以龍圖閣待制知溫州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Minister of Personnel; critics objected that Ni had never served in prefecture or county posts, so he was made Awaiting-Orders at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and Prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Minister of Personnel, but critics said Ni had never served in prefecture or county office, so he was made Awaiting-Orders at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and Prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使孟庾總師討閩寇，過郡，擬趣使赴援。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Meng Yu commanded the army in suppressing the Fujian bandits and passed through the prefecture; Ni urged him to hurry to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Meng Yu led the army against the Fujian bandits and passed through the prefecture; Ni urged him to hurry to its relief.

sentences.zh: 庾怒，命擬犒師。

translations.literal: Yu grew angry and ordered Ni to supply the army with rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Yu grew angry and ordered Ni to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 擬借封椿錢用之，已乃自劾。

translations.literal: Ni borrowed funds from the sealed treasury reserve to do so, then impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ni borrowed funds from the sealed treasury reserve to do so, then impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加秩一等，召為禮部尚書，遷吏部。

translations.literal: When the bandits were suppressed he received one increment in rank, was summoned as Minister of Rites, and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were suppressed he received one step in rank, was summoned as Minister of Rites, and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 渡江後，法無見籍，吏隨事立文，號為「省記」，出入自如。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangtze there were no surviving law codes on the books; clerks improvised documents case by case, called 'Provincial Records,' and passed in and out at will.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangtze there were no law codes still on the books; clerks improvised documents case by case in what was called "Provincial Records," coming and going at will.

sentences.zh: 至是修《七司敕令》，命擬總之，以舊法及續降指揮詳定成書，上之。

translations.literal: At this time the Seven Departments Statutes and Orders were revised; Ni was ordered to oversee the task. Using old laws and successive supplemental commands, he worked out a detailed text and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Seven Departments Statutes and Orders were revised; Ni was ordered to oversee the work. Using old laws and successive supplemental commands, he worked out a detailed text and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 金人再攻淮，詔日輪侍從赴都堂，給劄問以攻守之策。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens again attacked the Huai region, an edict ordered members of the Secretariat and Attendant-in-Waiting to rotate daily to the Hall of State Affairs, each given a note asking for offensive and defensive strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens again attacked the Huai region, an edict ordered members of the Secretariat and Attendants-in-Waiting to rotate daily to the Hall of State Affairs, each given a note asking for offensive and defensive strategy.

sentences.zh: 擬言：「國勢強則戰，將士勇則戰，財用足則戰，我為主、彼為客則戰。

translations.literal: Ni said: 'When national strength is strong one can fight; when officers and soldiers are brave one can fight; when finances are ample one can fight; when we are host and they guest one can fight.
translations.idiomatic: Ni said, "When national strength is strong one can fight; when officers and soldiers are brave one can fight; when finances are ample one can fight; when we are host and they guest one can fight.

sentences.zh: 陛下移蹕東南，前年幸會稽，今年幸臨安，興王之居，未有定議非如高祖在關中、光武在河內也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has moved the court southeast; the year before last you visited Kuaiji, this year Lin'an—yet the place where a dynasty founding its rule should reside has not been settled. This is not like Gaozu of Han in Guanzhong or Guangwu in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has moved the court southeast—last year to Kuaiji, this year to Lin'an—yet the seat from which a dynasty should rise has not been settled. This is not like Gaozu of Han in Guanzhong or Guangwu in Henei.

sentences.zh: 以國勢論之，可言守，未可言戰。」

translations.literal: Judging by national strength, one can speak of defense—not yet of war.'
translations.idiomatic: Judging by national strength, one can speak of defense—not yet of war."

sentences.zh: 擬謂時相姑議戰以示武，實不能戰也。

translations.literal: Ni said the chief minister for the moment talked of war to display martial spirit, but in fact could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Ni said the chief minister for the moment talked of war to show martial spirit, but in fact could not fight.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，以天旱地震詔群臣言事，擬奏曰：「法行公，則人樂而氣和；

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, an earthquake during drought prompted an edict calling on all officials to speak their minds. Ni memorialized: 'When law is applied impartially, people are content and the atmosphere harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaoxing, drought and earthquake prompted an edict calling on all officials to speak freely. Ni memorialized, "When law is applied impartially, people are content and the atmosphere harmonious.

sentences.zh: 行之偏，則人怨而氣乖。

translations.literal: When it is applied with partiality, people resent it and the atmosphere turns discordant.
translations.idiomatic: When it is applied with partiality, people resent it and the atmosphere turns discordant.

sentences.zh: 試以小事論之：比者監司、守臣獻羨餘則黜之，宣撫司獻則受之，是行法止及疏遠也。

translations.literal: Take a small matter: lately when circuit intendant-commissioners and prefectural officers presented surplus revenue they were dismissed, but when the Pacification Commission presented surplus revenue it was accepted—this is applying the law only to the remote and insignificant.
translations.idiomatic: Take a small matter: lately when circuit commissioners and prefects presented surplus revenue they were dismissed, but when the Pacification Commission presented surplus revenue it was accepted—this is applying the law only to the remote and insignificant.

sentences.zh: 有自庶僚為侍從者，臥家視職，未嘗入謝，遂得美職而去，若鼓院官移疾廢朝謁，則斥罷之，是行法止及冗賤也。

translations.literal: Some who rose from junior offices to Attendants-in-Waiting remained at home fulfilling their duties without ever entering court to thank the throne, yet obtained fine posts and departed; yet if a drum-court official pleaded illness and skipped court audience, he was dismissed—this is applying the law only to the redundant and lowly.
translations.idiomatic: Some who rose from junior offices to Attendants-in-Waiting stayed home on duty without ever entering court to give thanks, yet obtained fine posts and left; yet if a drum-court official pleaded illness and missed court audience, he was dismissed—this is applying the law only to the redundant and lowly.

sentences.zh: 榷酤立法甚嚴，犯者籍家財充賞，大官勢臣連營列障，公行酤賣則不敢問，是行法止及孤弱也。

translations.literal: The monopoly law on wine was extremely strict; violators had their family property confiscated as reward; yet great officials and powerful clans linked their compounds in rows and sold wine openly without anyone daring to investigate—this is applying the law only to the isolated and weak.
translations.idiomatic: The wine monopoly law was extremely strict; violators had their family property confiscated as reward; yet great officials and powerful clans lined their compounds in rows and sold wine openly without anyone daring to investigate—this is applying the law only to the isolated and weak.

sentences.zh: 小事如此，推而極之，則怨多而和氣傷矣。」

translations.literal: In small matters it is thus; extend this to the extreme and resentment will multiply and harmony will be injured.'
translations.idiomatic: In small matters it is thus; extend this to the extreme and resentment will multiply and harmony will be injured."

sentences.zh: 尋以言者罷為徽猷閣直學士、提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Before long, because of criticism, he was dismissed and made Direct Academic of the Huaiyou Hall and Director of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because of criticism, he was dismissed and made Direct Academic of the Huaiyou Hall and Director of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，擬兄子駕部郎官興祖與擬上封事侵在位者，故父子俱罷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ni's nephew Xing Zu, an official in the Transport Bureau, and Ni himself had submitted sealed memorials offending those in power; therefore father and nephew were both dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ni's nephew Xing Zu, an official in the Transport Bureau, and Ni himself had submitted sealed memorials offending those in power; therefore uncle and nephew were both dismissed.

sentences.zh: 起知溫州，提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: He was later recalled as Prefect of Wenzhou and Director of the Mingdao Abbey in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as Prefect of Wenzhou and Director of the Mingdao Abbey in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，諡「文憲」。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-five; his posthumous title was "Wenxian."
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five; his posthumous title was "Wenxian."

sentences.zh: 初，擬自海州還居鎮江。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ni returned from Haizhou he settled in Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ni returned from Haizhou he settled in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 趙萬叛兵逼郡，守臣趙子崧戰敗，遁去。

translations.literal: Zhao Wan's mutinous troops pressed upon the prefecture; the prefect Zhao Zisong was defeated in battle and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wan's mutinous troops pressed upon the prefecture; Prefect Zhao Zisong was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 擬挾母出避，遇賊至，欲兵之，擬曰：「死無所避，願勿驚老母。」

translations.literal: Ni took his mother and went out to escape; when bandits arrived and wished to use force against them, Ni said: 'Death cannot be avoided; I only ask that you not frighten my aged mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Ni took his mother and fled; when bandits arrived and wished to use force, Ni said, "Death cannot be avoided—I only ask that you not frighten my aged mother."

sentences.zh: 賊舍之。

translations.literal: The bandits let them go.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits let them go.

sentences.zh: 他賊又至，臨以刃，擬指其母曰：「此吾母也，幸勿怖之。」

translations.literal: Other bandits came again and held blades to them; Ni pointed to his mother and said: 'This is my mother; please do not frighten her.'
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits came again and held blades to them; Ni pointed to his mother and said, "This is my mother—please do not frighten her."

sentences.zh: 賊又舍去。

translations.literal: Those bandits too let them go.
translations.idiomatic: Those bandits too let them go.

sentences.zh: 有《淨智先生集》及《注杜甫詩》二十卷。

translations.literal: He had the Collected Works of Master Jingzhi and a twenty-volume Commentary on Du Fu's Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Collected Works of Master Jingzhi and a twenty-volume Commentary on Du Fu's Poetry.

sentences.zh: 趙逵，字莊叔，其先秦人，八世祖處榮徙蜀，家於資州。

translations.literal: Zhao Kui, courtesy name Zhuangshu, was descended from Qin people; his eighth-generation ancestor Churong moved to Shu and settled in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kui, courtesy name Zhuangshu, was descended from people of Qin; his eighth-generation ancestor Churong moved to Shu and settled in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 逵讀書數行俱下，尤好聚古書，考歷代興衰治亂之跡，與當代名人鉅公出處大節，根窮底究，尚友其人。

translations.literal: Kui read several lines at a glance and especially loved collecting ancient books, examining the traces of rise and fall, order and disorder through the ages, and the great integrity of contemporary eminent men in their coming forward and withdrawal—he traced matters to their roots and made such men his friends across time.
translations.idiomatic: Kui could read several lines at a glance and especially loved collecting ancient books, tracing the rise and fall of dynasties through the ages and the great integrity of eminent men in their coming forward and withdrawal; he pursued matters to their roots and made such men his friends across time.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十年，類省奏名，明年對策，論君臣父子之情甚切，擢第一。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Shaoxing he was listed in the provincial examination; the next year in the palace examination he argued the feelings between ruler and minister, father and son with great urgency, and was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Shaoxing he was listed in the provincial examination; the next year in the palace examination he argued the bond between ruler and minister, father and son with great urgency, and was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜意有所屬，而逵對獨當帝意，檜不悅。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui had someone he favored in mind, but Kui's answers alone matched the Emperor's intention; Qin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui had someone else in mind, but Kui's answers alone matched the Emperor's intention; Qin was displeased.

sentences.zh: 即罷知舉王曮，授逵左承事郎、簽書劍南東川。

translations.literal: He immediately dismissed Wang Yan from the examination office and appointed Kui Left Officer of the Secretariat and Secretariat Officer of the Eastern Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dismissed Wang Yan from the examination office and appointed Kui Left Officer of the Secretariat and Secretariat Officer of the Eastern Sichuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問檜，趙逵安在？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Qin, 'Where is Zhao Kui?'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once asked Qin, "Where is Zhao Kui?"

sentences.zh: 檜以實對。

translations.literal: Qin answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Qin answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝又問，除校書郎。

translations.literal: After a long time the Emperor asked again, and Kui was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the Emperor asked again, and Kui was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 逵單車赴闕，徵稅者希檜意，搜行橐皆書籍，才數金而已。

translations.literal: Kui came alone to court in a single cart; the tax collector, hoping to please Qin, searched his luggage—all books, only a few pieces of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Kui came alone to court in a single cart; the tax collector, hoping to please Qin, searched his luggage—all books, only a few pieces of gold.

sentences.zh: 既就職，未嘗私謁，檜意愈恨。

translations.literal: Once in office he never paid private visits; Qin resented him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he never paid private visits; Qin resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 逵賡御制《芝草詩》，有「皇心未敢宴安圖」之句，檜見之怒曰：「逵猶以為未太平耶？」

translations.literal: Kui continued the imperial poem on lingzhi grass with the line 'The imperial heart dares not yet seek ease and pleasure.' When Qin saw it he said angrily: 'Does Kui still think the realm is not yet at peace?'
translations.idiomatic: Kui continued the imperial poem on lingzhi grass with the line "The imperial heart dares not yet seek ease and pleasure." When Qin saw it he said angrily, "Does Kui still think the realm is not yet at peace?"

sentences.zh: 又謂逵曰：「館中祿薄，能以家來乎？」

translations.literal: He also said to Kui: 'The stipend in the Secretariat is thin—can you bring your family here?'
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Kui, "The stipend in the Secretariat is thin—can you bring your family here?"

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「親老不能涉險遠。」

translations.literal: Kui said: 'My parents are old and cannot travel far through dangerous country.'
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "My parents are old and cannot travel far through dangerous country."

sentences.zh: 檜徐曰：「當以百金為助。」

translations.literal: Qin said slowly: 'Then I shall assist you with a hundred pieces of gold.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin said slowly, "Then I shall assist you with a hundred pieces of gold."

sentences.zh: 逵唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Kui could only assent.
translations.idiomatic: Kui could only assent.

sentences.zh: 又遣所親申前言，諷逵往謝，逵不答，檜滋怒，欲擠之，未及而死。

translations.literal: Qin again sent a close associate to repeat the earlier suggestion, hinting that Kui should come to thank him; Kui did not respond, and Qin grew angrier still and wished to squeeze him out, but had not yet done so when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qin again sent a close associate to repeat the earlier suggestion, hinting that Kui should come to thank him; Kui did not respond, and Qin grew angrier still and wished to squeeze him out, but had not yet done so when he died.

sentences.zh: 帝臨哭檜還，即遷逵著作佐郎兼權禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from weeping at Qin's bier, Kui was immediately promoted to Associate Editor and acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned from weeping at Qin's bier, Kui was immediately promoted to Associate Editor and acting Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝如景靈宮，秘省起居惟逵一人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went to the Jingling Palace, among the Secretariat attendants recording imperial actions, only Kui was present.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor went to the Jingling Palace, among the Secretariat attendants recording imperial actions, only Kui was present.

sentences.zh: 帝屢目逵，即日命引見上殿，帝迎謂曰：「卿知之乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor looked at Kui several times, and that same day ordered him summoned to the upper hall. The Emperor greeted him saying: 'Do you know?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor looked at Kui several times, and that same day ordered him summoned to the upper hall. The Emperor greeted him, saying, "Do you know?

sentences.zh: 始終皆朕自擢。

translations.literal: From beginning to end it was I who raised you.
translations.idiomatic: From beginning to end it was I who raised you.

sentences.zh: 自卿登第後，為大臣沮格，久不見卿。

translations.literal: After you passed the examination, great ministers blocked your advancement, and I did not see you for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: After you passed the examination, great ministers blocked your advancement, and I did not see you for a long time.

sentences.zh: 秦檜日薦士，未嘗一語及卿，以此知卿不附權貴，真天子門生也。」

translations.literal: Qin Hui daily recommended men, yet never once mentioned you—I know from this that you do not attach yourself to the powerful. You are truly a disciple of the Son of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui daily recommended men, yet never once mentioned you—I know from this that you do not attach yourself to the powerful. You are truly a disciple of the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 詔充普安郡王府教授。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him instructor to the Prince of Pu'an's household.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him instructor to the Prince of Pu'an's household.

sentences.zh: 逵奏：「言路久不通，乞廣賜開納，勿以微賤為間，庶幾養成敢言之氣。」

translations.literal: Kui memorialized: 'The path of remonstrance has long been blocked; I beg that it be opened more widely, and that no one be excluded for being humble and lowly, so that a spirit of daring to speak may be cultivated.'
translations.idiomatic: Kui memorialized, "The path of remonstrance has long been blocked; I beg that it be opened more widely, and that no one be excluded for being humble and lowly, so that a spirit of daring to speak may be cultivated."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 普安府勸講至戾太子事，王曰：「于斯時也，斬江充自歸於武帝，何如？」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Pu'an's household lectured on the affair of the Heir Apparent Li, the prince said: 'At that time, if the heir had beheaded Jiang Chong and surrendered himself to Emperor Wu, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Pu'an's household lectured on the affair of the Heir Apparent Li, the prince said, "At that time, if the heir had beheaded Jiang Chong and surrendered himself to Emperor Wu, what then?"

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「此非臣子所能。」

translations.literal: Kui said: 'That is not something a subject can do.'
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "That is not something a subject can do."

sentences.zh: 王意蓋有所在也。

translations.literal: The prince's meaning presumably lay elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's meaning presumably lay elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷著作郎，尋除起居郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Editor, and soon appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Editor, and soon appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 入謝，帝又曰：「秦檜炎炎，不附者惟卿一人。」

translations.literal: When he entered to thank the throne, the Emperor again said: 'When Qin Hui blazed with power, you alone did not attach yourself to him.'
translations.idiomatic: When he entered to thank the throne, the Emperor again said, "When Qin Hui blazed with power, you alone did not attach yourself to him."

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「臣不能效古人抗折權姦，但不與之同爾，然所以事宰相禮亦不敢闕。」

translations.literal: Kui said: 'Your servant cannot imitate the ancients in resisting and breaking powerful favorites, but simply will not join them—that said, in serving the chief minister I do not dare omit proper ritual either.'
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "Your servant cannot imitate the ancients in resisting and breaking powerful favorites, but simply will not join them—that said, in serving the chief minister I do not dare omit proper ritual either."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「受陛下爵祿而奔走權門，臣不惟不敢，亦且不忍。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'Having received rank and stipend from Your Majesty yet rushing to the doors of the powerful—your servant not only dares not, but could not bear to.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Having received rank and stipend from Your Majesty yet rushing to the doors of the powerful—your servant not only dares not, but could not bear to."

sentences.zh: 明年同知貢舉，盡公考閱，以革舊弊，遂得王十朋、閻安中。

translations.literal: The next year he served as co-supervisor of the examinations, examining entirely by public merit to reform old abuses, and thus obtained Wang Shipeng and Yan Anzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as co-supervisor of the examinations, examining entirely by public merit to reform old abuses, and thus obtained Wang Shipeng and Yan Anzhong.

sentences.zh: 始，逵未出貢闈，蔣璨除戶部侍郎，給事中辛次膺以璨交結希進，還之。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Kui left the examination hall, Jiang Can was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue; Supervising Secretary Xin Ciying returned the appointment because Jiang had cultivated connections seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Kui left the examination hall, Jiang Can was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue; Supervising Secretary Xin Ciying returned the appointment because Jiang had cultivated connections seeking advancement.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，罷次膺，付逵書讀，逵不可，璨以此出知蘇州，次膺仍得次對，逵兼給事中。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and dismissed Ciying, handing the document to Kui to read; Kui refused. Because of this Jiang was sent out as Prefect of Suzhou, while Ciying still received sequential audiences; Kui was given concurrent appointment as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry and dismissed Ciying, handing the document to Kui to read; Kui refused. Because of this Jiang was sent out as Prefect of Suzhou, while Ciying still received sequential audiences; Kui was given concurrent appointment as Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除中書舍人，登第六年而當外制，南渡後所未有也。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Drafting Drafter of the Secretariat and Chancellery; in the sixth year after passing the examination he reached the outer-drafting post—unprecedented since the move south.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Drafting Drafter of the Secretariat and Chancellery; in the sixth year after passing the examination he reached the outer-drafting post—unprecedented since the move south.

sentences.zh: 帝語王綸曰：「趙逵純正可用，朕於蜀士未見其比。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Wang Lun: 'Zhao Kui is upright and can be used; among Sichuan scholars I have seen none to match him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Wang Lun, "Zhao Kui is upright and can be used; among Sichuan scholars I have seen none to match him.

sentences.zh: 朕所以甫二歲令至此，報其不附權貴也。」

translations.literal: That is why after only two years I brought him to this position—to reward his refusal to attach himself to the powerful.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why after only two years I brought him to this position—to reward his refusal to attach himself to the powerful."

sentences.zh: 先是，逵嘗薦杜莘老、唐文若、孫道夫皆蜀名士，至是奉詔舉士，又以馮方、劉儀鳳、李石、郯次雲應詔，宰執以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier Kui had recommended Du Xinlao, Tang Wenruo, and Sun Daofu, all famous Sichuan scholars; now by edict he recommended gentlemen, and also recommended Feng Fang, Liu Yifeng, Li Shi, and Tan Ciyun in response to the summons; the chief ministers reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kui had recommended Du Xinlao, Tang Wenruo, and Sun Daofu, all famous Sichuan scholars; now by edict he recommended gentlemen, and also recommended Feng Fang, Liu Yifeng, Li Shi, and Tan Ciyun in response to the summons; the chief ministers reported this.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蜀人道遠，其間文學行義有用者，不因論薦無由得知。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Sichuan is far; among its scholars useful in learning and integrity there are many who, without recommendation and discussion, could never be known.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Sichuan is far; among its scholars useful in learning and integrity there are many who, without recommendation and discussion, could never be known.

sentences.zh: 前此蜀中宦遊者多隔絕，不得一至朝廷，甚可惜也。」

translations.literal: Previously many who served in office in Sichuan were cut off and could never once reach court—most regrettable.'
translations.idiomatic: Previously many who served in office in Sichuan were cut off and could never once reach court—most regrettable."

sentences.zh: 自檜顓權，深抑蜀士，故帝語及之。

translations.literal: Since Qin monopolized power he deeply suppressed Sichuan scholars; therefore the Emperor spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin monopolized power he deeply suppressed Sichuan scholars; therefore the Emperor spoke of this.

sentences.zh: 逵以疾求外，帝命國醫王繼先視疾，不可為矣。

translations.literal: Kui, citing illness, requested an outside appointment; the Emperor ordered Court Physician Wang Jixian to examine him, but nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, citing illness, requested an outside appointment; the Emperor ordered Court Physician Wang Jixian to examine him, but nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十一。

translations.literal: He died at forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝為之抆淚歎息。

translations.literal: The Emperor wiped away tears and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wiped away tears and sighed.

sentences.zh: 逵嘗自謂：「司馬溫公不近非色，不取非財，吾雖不肖，庶幾慕之。」

translations.literal: Kui once said of himself: 'Sima Wengong would not approach improper beauty or take improper wealth; though I am unworthy, I would fain emulate him.'
translations.idiomatic: Kui once said of himself, "Sima Wengong would not approach improper beauty or take improper wealth; though I am unworthy, I would fain emulate him."

sentences.zh: 方檜權盛時，忤檜者固非止逵一人，而帝亟稱逵不附麗，又謂逵文章似蘇軾，故稱為「小東坡」，未及用而逵死，惜其論建不傳於世。

translations.literal: When Qin's power was at its height, those who offended Qin were certainly not only Kui; yet the Emperor repeatedly praised Kui for not attaching himself, and also said Kui's literary style resembled Su Shi's—therefore he was called 'Little Su Dongpo.' Before he could be fully employed Kui died; it is a pity his policy proposals were not transmitted to the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin's power was at its height, those who offended Qin were certainly not only Kui; yet the Emperor repeatedly praised Kui for not attaching himself, and also said Kui's literary style resembled Su Shi's—therefore he was called "Little Su Dongpo." Before he could be fully employed Kui died; it is a pity his policy proposals were not transmitted to the world.

sentences.zh: 有《棲雲集》三十卷。

translations.literal: He had the Qiyun ji in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Qiyun ji in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 論曰：如圭師于安國，居正師于楊時，敦復師于程頤，表臣交于陳瓘，其師友淵源有自來矣。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Rugui took as master Hu Anguo; Juzheng took Yang Shi; Dunfu took Cheng Yi; Biaochen associated with Chen Guan—their masters and friends had provenance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Rugui took Hu Anguo as master; Juzheng took Yang Shi; Dunfu took Cheng Yi; Biaochen associated with Chen Guan—their teachers and friends had provenance.

sentences.zh: 故其議論讜直，剛嚴鯁峭，不惑異說，不畏強禦，大略相似。

translations.literal: Therefore their discussions were upright and frank, stern and uncompromising; they were not misled by heterodox teachings and did not fear the powerful; in broad outline they were much alike.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore their discussions were upright and frank, stern and uncompromising; they were not misled by heterodox teachings and did not fear the powerful; in broad outline they were much alike.

sentences.zh: 若夫居正辨王氏《三經》之繆，龜年首劾秦檜主和之非，程瑀力排蔡京之黨，尤為有功於名教。

translations.literal: As for Juzheng refuting the errors of Wang's Three Classics, Guinian being first to impeach Qin Hui for the wrong of advocating peace, and Cheng Yu forcefully driving out Cai Jing's faction—they were especially meritorious to the teaching of names and principles.
translations.idiomatic: As for Juzheng refuting the errors of Wang's Three Classics, Guinian being first to impeach Qin Hui for the wrong of advocating peace, and Cheng Yu forcefully driving out Cai Jing's faction—they were especially meritorious to the teaching of names and principles.

sentences.zh: 張闡論事無避，洪擬樸實端亮，趙逵純正善文，皆一時之良，為檜所忌而不撓者。

translations.literal: Zhang Chan remonstrated without evasion; Hong Ni was plain, solid, and upright; Zhao Kui was pure, correct, and skilled in letters—all worthy men of their age whom Qin resented yet who did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chan remonstrated without evasion; Hong Ni was plain, solid, and upright; Zhao Kui was pure, correct, and skilled in letters—all worthy men of their age whom Qin resented yet who did not bend.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「歲寒然後知松柏之後凋。」

translations.literal: The saying goes: 'Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither.'
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, "Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither."

sentences.zh: 信哉！

translations.literal: How true!
translations.idiomatic: How true!
